articles.title: Prefeitura prorroga Programa Tá Pago, Tá em Dia ISS | G1
articles.standfirst: Contribuintes têm até 31 de outubro para aderir ao programa, que oferece descontos de até 100% em juros e multas de dívidas de ISS, com opções de pagamento à vista ou parcelado.
articles.summary: Contribuintes têm até 31 de outubro para aderir ao programa, que oferece descontos de até 100% em juros e multas de dívidas de ISS, com opções de pagamento à vista ou parcelado.
articles.body:
A Prefeitura de São José dos Campos prorrogou para o dia 31 de outubro de 2026 o prazo de adesão ao Refis 2026, por meio do Programa Tá Pago, Tá em Dia ISS.

O programa prevê descontos para o pagamento do ISSQN (Imposto Sobre Serviço de Qualquer Natureza) lançado em dívida ativa este ano (executada ou não). O prazo anterior terminaria nesta quarta-feira (30).

O novo prazo consta do Decreto 20.373/26, publicado no Diário do Município desta segunda-feira (28). Os descontos continuam variando de 80% (para pagamento parcelado em até quatro vezes) a 100% (para pagamento à vista) nos juros e multas, além de remissão da correção monetária.

Podem usufruir do benefício pessoas físicas e jurídicas que se enquadrem nas condições apresentadas na Lei Complementar nº 720/2026, aprovada pela Câmara Municipal em agosto. Para ter direito aos descontos, o contribuinte deve aderir ao programa por meio de formulário eletrônico.

O contribuinte que aderir ao programa receberá a confirmação por e-mail e um link para o sistema de pagamento da dívida (à vista ou parcelado), que em breve estará disponível.

Não estão incluídos neste programa os créditos imobiliários, as multas não tributárias e multas de trânsito, as contribuições e as taxas de serviço público e poder de polícia.

Ao aderir ao programa, o contribuinte também assume as seguintes condições: confissão extrajudicial dos créditos abrangidos, aceitação plena e irretratável de todas as condições, renúncia a alegações de direito que fundamentem impugnações ou recursos, desistência de impugnações, defesas, recursos, ações judiciais e embargos à execução fiscal.

O contribuinte poderá ser excluído automaticamente do programa caso haja inadimplência de duas parcelas (consecutivas ou alternativas) ou atraso superior a 60 dias.

Neste caso, a dívida terá restabelecimento dos acréscimos legais originalmente devidos, prosseguimento da cobrança administrativa e judicial; e retomada da execução fiscal, protesto e demais medidas cabíveis.

articles.title: Nunes diz que reação à inundação no túnel do Anhangabaú 'funcionou bem', com água subindo 1 metro em 3 minutos | G1
articles.standfirst: Prefeito atribui enchente à intensidade da chuva, mas admite que pode revisar protocolo e ampliar número de bombas. Nível da água demorou cerca de uma hora para baixar completamente.
articles.summary: Prefeito atribui enchente à intensidade da chuva, mas admite que pode revisar protocolo e ampliar número de bombas. Nível da água demorou cerca de uma hora para baixar completamente.
articles.body:
O prefeito de São Paulo, Ricardo Nunes, durante entrevista coletiva sobre o alagamento no túnel do Anhangabaú — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

O prefeito de São Paulo, Ricardo Nunes (MDB), afirmou que a reação à enchente no túnel do Vale do Anhangabaú funcionou bem e que a água subiu 1 metro em apenas três minutos durante o temporal que atingiu a capital paulista na tarde de quarta-feira (14). A enchente deixou 26 carros e dois ônibus submersos.

"[O alagamento] começou às 16h07, e às 16h10, exatamente três minutos depois, você já tinha mais de um metro de lâmina d'água", afirmou nesta quinta-feira (15) durante entrevista coletiva.

Segundo a prefeitura, as seis bombas instaladas no local funcionaram ininterruptamente, sem apresentar falhas, mas não conseguiram dar vazão ao volume de chuva registrado na região. Demorou aproximadamente uma hora até que a inundação fosse eliminada.

De acordo com a administração municipal, choveu 42 milímetros na região do Anhangabaú em cerca de 40 minutos , o equivalente a 37% da média prevista para todo o mês de outubro na capital. A prefeitura informou que o volume corresponde ao esperado para 11 dias do mês.

Apesar do transtorno à população , Nunes avalia que a resposta da prefeitura ao episódio foi adequada diante das circunstâncias. "É um volume muito grande de água. [O protocolo de reação] funcionou bem. Pra você ver, com esse tanto de volume de água, ela demorou três minutos pra encher, e a gente conseguiu rapidamente, considerado o histórico que tem do Anhangabaú, fazer com que a água, voltasse à sua normalidade", declarou o prefeito.

Segundo o prefeito, o alagamento começou por volta das 16h07 e foi significativamente reduzido em menos de uma hora com o acionamento das bombas fixas do túnel e de caminhões equipados com bombas de sucção que reforçaram a operação. Nunes disse que os veículos emergenciais chegaram ao local por volta das 16h40.

Segundo ele, quando a precipitação mais intensa começou, o túnel já estava ocupado por veículos em horário de pico. "Infelizmente a gente não conseguiu se antecipar e fazer o bloqueio dos veículos para dentro do túnel, porque os carros já estavam lá quando o volume de água caiu", afirmou.

Homem observa interior de carro que foi atingido por inundação no túnel do Anhangabaú — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Apesar de avaliar que a resposta da administração municipal foi adequada, Nunes admitiu que os procedimentos poderão ser revistos após o episódio. "Agora a gente vai estar melhorando os nossos protocolos, talvez ampliar o volume das nossas bombas, isso tudo a gente vai estar fazendo", disse o prefeito, sem dar mais detalhes.

Mais cedo, a Companhia de Engenharia de Tráfego (CET) informou que as interdições do túnel começaram às 15h38, dentro do protocolo adotado em situações de Estado de Atenção para alagamentos .

O prefeito, porém, contestou a informação apresentada por repórteres durante a entrevista coletiva. "Não houve fechamento às 15h48 de ontem. Ou você está com a informação errada, ou a CET te passou a informação errada", afirmou.

Ao rebater questionamentos sobre a possibilidade de fechamento preventivo do túnel, o prefeito afirmou que a intensidade da chuva surpreendeu até os serviços de meteorologia e que os veículos já estavam dentro da via quando a água começou a subir.

"O protocolo funcionou. As pessoas também perguntaram: 'ah, mas por que não fechou o trânsito na hora que começou a chuva?' Se você olhar a previsão dos meteorologistas do dia anterior com relação à data de ontem, não tinha uma previsão desse volume de água", justificou o prefeito.

"Sequer os meteorologistas conseguiram prever aquele volume de água por conta das mudanças climáticas. Se você pegar o boletim do nosso Centro de Operações, ele falou o seguinte: 'olha, vai ter uma frente que vem do interior e vai ter chuvas de moderada a forte'. Quer dizer, de moderada a forte é um espaço gigantesco", acrescentou.

Carros e ônibus boiam no túnel do Anhangabaú durante chuva forte em SP — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

"A ação da prefeitura é muito rápida, automática. Agora, vamos ser sincero com todas as pessoas que moram em São Paulo ou que trabalham e que visitam. A gente vive um momento de mudança climática. Cair 40% da chuva prevista para o mês inteiro em poucos minutos? A gente obviamente tem uma situação que é diferente de um padrão normal", acrescentou.

O prefeito também atribuiu o alagamento à concentração de cursos d'água subterrâneos que convergem para a região e disse que avalia a construção de um piscinão embaixo do Terminal Bandeira, próximo ao Vale do Anhangabaú.

Segundo ele, a obra está estimada em mais de R$ 350 milhões, mas ainda não é considerada prioritária diante de outras intervenções contra enchentes em andamento na cidade.

articles.title: Houthis bombardeiam área do palácio presidencial no Iêmen | G1
articles.standfirst: Ataque do grupo terrorista iemenita é uma escalada na guerra travada contra forças governamentais do Iêmen, que são apoiadas pela Arábia Saudita.
articles.summary: Ataque do grupo terrorista iemenita é uma escalada na guerra travada contra forças governamentais do Iêmen, que são apoiadas pela Arábia Saudita.
articles.body:
O grupo terrorista Houthi bombardeou o complexo do palácio presidencial do Iêmen em Áden, no sul do país. O governo iemenita afirmou que o ataque matou dois seguranças, mas que primeiro-ministro está seguro.

Os Houthis utilizaram mísseis e drones no ataque, que atingiu um local próximo ao palácio presidencial e matou dois seguranças , afirmaram duas fontes do governo iemenita à agência de notícias Reuters.

O primeiro-ministro do Iêmen e integrantes do gabinete que estavam no complexo do palácio presidencial de Maashiq não ficaram feridos , afirmou o ministro da Informação, Moammar al-Eryani.

O ministro disse ainda que os Houthis dispararam cinco mísseis contra o local. Testemunhas afirmaram à agência Associated Press (AP) que ouviram ao menos seis explosões de grande magnitude.

Segundo a AP, duas das explosões ocorreram perto do topo da colina onde fica o Palácio Al-Mashiq, e o restante ocorreu perto do portão do complexo presidencial.

A agência de notícias Saba, controlada pelos Houthis, citou um militar que alegou que o grupo tinha como alvos um quartel-general de operações militares comandado por oficiais sauditas no complexo , além de depósitos de armas.

Um porta-voz militar dos Houthis, que são financiados pelo Irã, alegou que o ataque desta quinta foi contra o que descreveu como um quartel-general de operações militares sauditas em Áden, e que a investida integrava a política declarada do grupo de “atacar concentrações militares sauditas onde quer que estejam”.

O ataque desta quinta ocorre na esteira de uma guerra de duas frentes travada pelos Houthis contra a Arábia Saudita e contra as forças do governo internacionalmente reconhecido do Iêmen —que são aliados dos sauditas. Esse conflito voltou a aquecer recentemente por conta da guerra entre Estados Unidos e Irã, e vem se expandindo ao longo das últimas semanas.

articles.title: Papa Leão XIV nomeia dom Andreolli bispo da diocese de Ponta de Pedras | G1
articles.standfirst: Italiano e missionário Xaveriano, ele atuava como bispo auxiliar da arquidiocese de Belém. CNBB enviou saudação ao novo bispo.
articles.summary: Italiano e missionário Xaveriano, ele atuava como bispo auxiliar da arquidiocese de Belém. CNBB enviou saudação ao novo bispo.
articles.body:
Papa Leão XIV nomeia dom Paulo Andreolli bispo da diocese de Ponta de Pedras, no Marajó. — Foto: Reprodução / Arquidiocese de Belém

O Papa Leão XIV nomeou, nesta quinta-feira (15), dom Paulo Andreolli bispo da diocese de Ponta de Pedras , no arquipélago do Marajó, no Pará. Com a nomeação, ele deixa o ofício de bispo auxiliar da arquidiocese de Belém.

Dom Paulo é italiano, missionário Xaveriano e se dedica ao trabalho pastoral, missionário e vocacional, com forte presença no Brasil, especialmente no Pará. Com a nomeação, ele se tornou o quarto bispo da diocese de Ponta de Pedras.

A Conferência Nacional dos Bispos do Brasil (CNBB) enviou saudação ao religioso. Na mensagem, a entidade afirmou que recebeu a notícia "com alegria" e expressou o desejo de que a nova etapa do pastoreio "fortaleça ainda mais a sua presença como discípulo missionário a serviço do povo de Deus do norte do nosso país".

Dom Paulo Andreolli nasceu em 16 de dezembro de 1972, em Pojana Maggiore, Vicenza, na Itália. É filho de Mario Andreolli e Giuliana Conte e tem duas irmãs, Elena e Laura.

Aos 11 anos, em 1984, ingressou no Seminário Xaveriano de Vicenza, onde concluiu o ensino médio. Entre 1992 e 1994, realizou o noviciado em Ancona e, em seguida, estudou filosofia e teologia na Casa Mãe dos Xaverianos, em Parma.

Ele fez os votos perpétuos em 5 de março de 2000, virou diácono no dia seguinte e se tornou padre em 17 de setembro de 2000.

A primeira destinação pastoral foi na comunidade formativa de Desio, em Milão, na Itália, onde atuou como animador vocacional e missionário. No período, cursou pós-graduação em espiritualidade e acompanhamento espiritual na Faculdade da Itália Setentrional, em Milão.

Em 17 de novembro de 2007, foi enviado ao Brasil. Atuou no Pará como vigário paroquial por cinco anos na cidade de São Félix do Xingu e como pároco por quatro anos em Tucumã, na atual Prelazia do Alto Xingu – Tucumã, com intensa dedicação aos jovens.

A partir de 2017, seguiu na missão como animador vocacional e missionário na região do Pará, com atuação na comunidade formativa de Ananindeua e junto ao Conselho Missionário Regional – Pará e Amapá (COMIRE). Também atuou como conselheiro regional dos Xaverianos e colaborou com a Conferência dos Religiosos do Brasil (CRB – Subnúcleo 2), em Belém.

Em 1º de fevereiro de 2023, o Papa Francisco nomeou padre Paulo Andreolli bispo auxiliar da arquidiocese de Belém do Pará, e atribuiu a ele também o título de bispo titular de Altava.

A ordenação episcopal aconteceu em 15 de abril de 2023, na catedral metropolitana de Belém, em cerimônia presidida por dom Alberto Taveira Corrêa, arcebispo de Belém. Com a consagração, ele se tornou o oitavo bispo auxiliar da arquidiocese.

articles.title: Dying in Detention
articles.summary: Fault Lines investigates the soaring death rates in immigration detention centres following President Trump’s crackdown.
articles.body:
In September 2025, 39-year-old Ismael Ayala-Uribe died just one month after entering California’s Adelanto ICE Processing Center.

He was one of more than 50 people to die in immigration custody during Donald Trump’s first 500 days back in office.

His family says he repeatedly complained of intense pain and asked for medical help, but received little beyond Tylenol. When he finally reached a hospital, his heart stopped within minutes.

The Trump administration is detaining record numbers of immigrants, and deaths in custody are soaring. Fault Lines investigates failures in medical care and oversight, allegations of retaliation against hunger strikers and the role of private prison companies in the rapid expansion of immigration detention.

articles.title: Acusado de matar ex-namorada na saída de academia vai a júri em Belém | G1
articles.standfirst: Crime aconteceu em 2019. Defesa alega atuação de grupo de extermínio, enquanto promotoria apresenta mensagens de ameaça enviadas pelo réu.
articles.summary: Crime aconteceu em 2019. Defesa alega atuação de grupo de extermínio, enquanto promotoria apresenta mensagens de ameaça enviadas pelo réu.
articles.body:
Teve início, na manhã desta quinta-feira, 15, o julgamento de Carlos Rafael da Silva Quintal, acusado de assassinar a tiros a ex-namorada , Raiana Brito, em março de 2019.

O crime aconteceu no bairro do Guamá , em Belém , no momento em que a jovem, de 21 anos, saía de uma academia. Segundo as investigações, o réu cometeu o crime por não aceitar o fim do relacionamento.

De acordo com depoimentos, Raiana e Carlos Rafael se conheceram em uma loja onde trabalhavam juntos. O namoro foi marcado por conflitos constantes.

A acusação, liderada pelo Ministério Público, apresentou capturas de tela (prints) do celular da vítima mostrando mensagens com ameaças de morte logo após o término do namoro.

Já a defesa de Carlos sustenta a tese de que Raiana teria sido vítima de grupos de extermínio que atuavam na região do Guamá na época do ocorrido.

A família de Raiana acompanha o julgamento no fórum de Belém que segue em andamento.

articles.title: Governo suspende autorizações para queimadas por 15 dias em Roraima | G1
articles.standfirst: Medida proíbe temporariamente uso do fogo em áreas rurais para tentar conter incêndios devido à estiagem causada pelo fenômeno El Niño. Femarh monitora descumprimentos.
articles.summary: Medida proíbe temporariamente uso do fogo em áreas rurais para tentar conter incêndios devido à estiagem causada pelo fenômeno El Niño. Femarh monitora descumprimentos.
articles.body:
Autorizações para queimadas em Roraima são suspensas por 15 dias, devido ao El Ni — Foto: Diane Sampaio/PMBV

O governo de Roraima suspendeu as autorizações para uso do fogo controlado no estado . A medida foi anunciada em coletiva nesta quinta-feira (15), em Boa Vista e vale por 15 dias . A restrição visa frear os incêndios durante a seca extrema que atinge o estado .

Com a decisão, as licenças para produtores rurais usarem o fogo para limpar pastos e áreas de plantio ficam paralisadas . O Comitê Estadual de Queimadas tomou a decisão por unanimidade . O grupo deve reavaliar o cenário em dez dias para definir os próximos passos, conforme a evolução do clima.

O presidente da Fundação Estadual do Meio Ambiente e Recursos Hídricos (Femarh), Wagner Severo, reforçou que, com o calendário suspenso temporariamente, qualquer tipo de queimada passa a ser considerada crime ambiental .

"A partir desse período, todos os focos de calor que forem detectados serão considerados ilegais, e aí serão adotadas as medidas administrativas cabíveis, do ponto de vista cível e penal", afirmou Severo.

Para identificar infratores, a Femarh vai usar um sistema de monitoramento que cruza a localização dos incêndios com o Cadastro Ambiental Rural (CAR). Na prática, o governo consegue saber exatamente em qual propriedade o fogo começou e quem é o dono da terra.

Segundo Severo, o objetivo da suspensão rigorosa é evitar que Roraima chegue à mesma situação de emergência do estado vizinho, o Amazonas.

O estado enfrenta uma alta expressiva nos incêndios . O Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais (Inpe) registrou 174 focos de calor apenas nas duas primeiras semanas de outubro . O número é 248% maior que o registrado no mesmo período do ano passado. Roraima já acumula 2.149 focos de calor em 2026 .

Rorainópolis , Pacaraima e Caracaraí lideram os registros de queimadas neste mês. A combinação de fogo e estiagem prolongada preocupa as autoridades e agrava os danos ambientais.

O meteorologista da Fundação Estadual do Meio Ambiente e Recursos Hídricos (Femarh), Ramon Alves, explicou que o estado enfrenta um fenômeno El Niño de categoria "muito forte" , um dos mais intensos registrados desde 1950.

"Além do nosso período seco, que já é intenso e começa agora em outubro, nós estamos acumulando esse fenômeno. As precipitações diminuíram bastante", destacou o especialista. Em agosto, por exemplo, choveu apenas 19 milímetros no estado, quando a média histórica é de 200 milímetros.

O impacto da falta de chuvas também é visível nos rios . O coordenador estadual da Defesa Civil, coronel Anderson Carvalho de Matos, informou que o nível do rio Branco chegou a apenas 52 centímetros de profundidade .

"O nosso rio baixou 1,60 metro nestes primeiros 15 dias de outubro. É muita coisa. Se seguirmos a tendência para os próximos sete dias, ele deve baixar mais 25 centímetros", alertou o coronel.

Para tentar reduzir os danos, o governo vai instalar quatro bases avançadas de fiscalização no interior a partir da próxima segunda-feira (19). O foco atual é orientar produtores rurais e atuar na prevenção, com apoio de associações e prefeituras.

A seca, intensificada pelo fenômeno El Niño, afeta diretamente a economia local. A Associação dos Produtores de Soja de Roraima (Aprosoja) projeta uma perda de 50% na produtividade da atual safra de grãos. O estado está em situação de emergência desde setembro .

Medida que suspende queimadas no estado foi anunciada em coletiva nesta quinta-feira (15). — Foto: Naamã Mourão/Rede Amazônica

Para reduzir os impactos da seca, a Companhia de Águas e Esgotos de Roraima (Caer) anunciou a perfuração de novos poços de água no estado . Em Boa Vista, a empresa planeja instalar uma bomba extra no rio Branco caso o nível da água chegue a uma situação crítica. Atualmente, a capital é abastecida por três estações de tratamento e 110 poços.

No interior, a distribuição deve ganhar o reforço de caminhões-pipa e novas estruturas de captação. As medidas incluem municípios como Rorainópolis, Caroebe e Pacaraima, além das vilas Félix Pinto (Cantá) e Vista Alegre (Caracaraí).

Na área da saúde, a Secretaria de Estado da Saúde (Sesau) prepara a rede de atendimento para os efeitos da fumaça e da estiagem. O foco é garantir o tratamento de pacientes com desidratação, doenças respiratórias e queimaduras.

articles.summary: Imagens mostram veículo de carga invadindo pista em alta velocidade antes do acidente. Samu enviou sete ambulâncias para o local.
articles.body:
Ao menos nove pessoas ficaram feridas depois que um caminhão desgovernado bateu num ônibus, na tarde desta quinta-feira (15), na PE-15, em Paulista , no Grande Recife. Imagens de uma câmera de segurança, enviadas à TV Globo , registraram o veículo de carga invadindo a pista em alta velocidade momentos antes do acidente (veja vídeo acima) .

Equipes do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) e do Corpo de Bombeiros foram acionadas para socorrer as vítimas. O Samu enviou sete ambulâncias ao local.

A batida aconteceu por volta das 15h, nas imediações do Terminal Integrado Pelópidas Silveira. Segundo testemunhas, o ônibus transportava funcionários de uma fábrica de carros quando foi atingido pelo caminhão.

No vídeo gravado pela câmera de segurança, é possível ver o caminhão saindo de uma rua perpendicular para cruzar a rodovia, fazendo os outros carros pararem no meio da estrada. O caminhão acabou atingindo o ônibus no outro sentido da pista.

Em imagens gravadas no local depois do acidente, é possível ver o coletivo tombado na rodovia. No canteiro central, ao lado do veículo caído, várias pessoas feridas ficaram sentadas, aguardando a chegada do Samu e dos bombeiros.

articles.title: Ex-IAS Divya Mittal launches own party: 10 civil servants who quit service to enter politics
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former IAS officer Divya Mittal on Thursday launched the Jan Neeti Bharat party and announced that it would contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former IAS officer Divya Mittal on Thursday launched the Jan Neeti Bharat party and announced that it would contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. Her announcement comes nearly a month after she took voluntary retirement from the civil services, ending a 13-year administrative career to pursue politics independently.In a video message on X, Mittal said the party will focus on making people central to policymaking and ensuring that the government remains accountable to them throughout its five-year term, rather than only on election day."Politics rules over you. In Jan Neeti, you will be the ones who rule," she said, announcing the party's name and its decision to contest the state polls due early next year.Her decision to launch a party of her own places her among a group of civil servants who left government service before their scheduled retirement to enter politics.Here are 10 former civil servants who made the transition from bureaucracy to politics before completing their service.1. Yashwant SinhaYashwant Sinha resigned from the Indian Administrative Service in 1984 to enter active politics. He joined the Janata Party and subsequently became associated with the Janata Dal before joining the BJP.Sinha first served as Union finance minister in the Chandra Shekhar government in 1990-91. Under Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, he returned to the finance ministry in 1998 and held the portfolio until 2002, when he became external affairs minister.His political career also included membership of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. Sinha later distanced himself from the BJP and joined the Trinamool Congress in 2021, before contesting the 2022 presidential election as the opposition's joint candidate.2. Ajit JogiAjit Jogi left the IAS in 1986 to enter politics and joined the Congress. He had served as a district collector before moving into political life and was subsequently elected to the Rajya Sabha.Jogi's biggest political breakthrough came in 2000, when Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh. He became the newly created state's first chief minister, holding office until 2003.After years in the Congress, Jogi broke away from the party in 2016 and founded the Janata Congress Chhattisgarh, seeking to establish an independent regional political platform.His career stands out as an example of a former administrator moving from district-level governance to the leadership of a newly formed state and later attempting to build a party of his own.3. Mani Shankar AiyarMani Shankar Aiyar resigned from the Indian Foreign Service in 1989 to enter politics. He had served as a diplomat for more than two decades and spent part of his career on deputation to the Prime Minister's Office under Rajiv Gandhi.Aiyar joined the Congress and won the Mayiladuthurai Lok Sabha seat in Tamil Nadu in 1991. He went on to become a prominent party leader and served as Union minister for petroleum and natural gas during the UPA government.He also held the panchayati raj portfolio and was involved in efforts to strengthen local self-government institutions.4. Arvind KejriwalArvind Kejriwal resigned from the Indian Revenue Service in 2006 after working in the income tax department. He had become involved in the Right to Information movement and founded the non-governmental organisation Parivartan to address citizens' grievances.His political journey gathered momentum during the Ana Hazare-led India Against Corruption movement, which campaigned for a stronger anti-corruption law. In 2012, Kejriwal founded the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), choosing to build a political organisation rather than join an established party.AAP made its electoral debut in the 2013 Delhi assembly elections, when Kejriwal defeated then chief minister Sheila Dikshit. He became Delhi chief minister in December 2013 and returned to the post after the party's victories in 2015 and 2020.5. KJ AlphonsKJ Alphons took voluntary retirement from the IAS in 2006 and entered electoral politics in Kerala. He contested the Kanjirappally assembly seat in Kerala as an independent candidate supported by the Left Democratic Front and won.Alphons later founded the Jana Shakti platform before joining the BJP in 2011. His political journey subsequently took him to Parliament, when he became a Rajya Sabha member.In 2017, he was inducted into the Narendra Modi government as Union minister of state for tourism, with independent charge, and also handled electronics and information technology.His transition from a civil servant known for urban development initiatives to a state-level politician and Union minister is an example of an officer moving across political formations during his career.6. Satyapal SinghSatyapal Singh, a 1980-batch IPS officer of the Maharashtra cadre, opted for voluntary retirement in January 2014 while serving as Mumbai police commissioner, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections.He joined the BJP and contested the Baghpat Lok Sabha seat in Uttar Pradesh in 2014, defeating Rashtriya Lok Dal chief Ajit Singh. He retained the constituency in the 2019 general election.Singh served as Union minister of state for human resource development and water resources during the Modi government's first term. Before entering politics, he had served in several police leadership roles and was known for his work in law enforcement.7. OP ChoudharyOP Choudhary, a 2005-batch IAS officer, resigned from the service in 2018 while serving as Raipur collector to enter politics. He joined the BJP and contested the Kharsia assembly constituency in Chhattisgarh in the same year.Choudhary lost that election but returned to the electoral contest in 2023, this time winning the Raipur City South seat. He was subsequently inducted into the Chhattisgarh government as a minister.His career highlights the uncertain transition from administration to politics. Unlike officers who win their first election, Choudhary's initial defeat did not end his political ambitions. He returned five years later and secured a place in the state Cabinet.8. Aparajita SarangiAparajita Sarangi, a 1994-batch IAS officer of the Odisha cadre, took voluntary retirement in 2018 while serving as joint secretary in the Union rural development ministry.She joined the BJP in November that year and contested the 2019 Lok Sabha election from Bhubaneswar. Sarangi won the seat, defeating Biju Janata Dal candidate Arup Patnaik.She retained the constituency in the 2024 general election, establishing herself as a BJP leader in Odisha.Sarangi's transition was particularly swift: she moved from a senior central government position to an electoral contest within months of leaving the service and subsequently secured two consecutive Lok Sabha victories.9. AK SharmaAK Sharma, a 1988-batch IAS officer of the Gujarat cadre, took voluntary retirement in January 2021, around 18 months before his scheduled superannuation.Sharma had spent a substantial part of his career working in the Prime Minister's Office and was associated with Narendra Modi's administration during his tenure as Gujarat chief minister and later as prime minister.After leaving the service, Sharma joined the BJP and was elected to the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council. He subsequently became a minister in the Yogi Adityanath government, handling portfolios including urban development and energy.His move demonstrated how a senior bureaucrat with experience in the central administration could enter state politics and secure a position in the Cabinet without first contesting a direct assembly election.10. Asim ArunAsim Arun, a 1994-batch IPS officer, took voluntary retirement in January 2022 while serving as Kanpur police commissioner. He joined the BJP soon afterwards, ahead of the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.Arun contested the Kannauj assembly seat and won, entering a constituency associated with the Samajwadi Party. He was subsequently inducted into the Yogi Adityanath government.His political entry came within weeks of his voluntary retirement, making him one of the clearest recent examples of a serving police officer moving directly into electoral politics before the end of his career.Bonus: K AnnamalaiK Annamalai, a 2011-batch IPS officer of the Karnataka cadre, resigned from the police service in September 2019, before completing his tenure. He had served as superintendent of police in Udupi and Chikkamagaluru districts before leaving the force.He joined the BJP in August 2020 and rose rapidly through the party's ranks. In July 2021, he was appointed the BJP's Tamil Nadu president, becoming one of the party's most prominent faces in the state.Annamalai contested the 2021 Tamil Nadu assembly election from Aravakurichi but lost to the DMK's R Elango. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, he contested from Coimbatore but lost to DMK candidate Ganapathi P Rajkumar.In June 2026, Annamalai quit the BJP following differences with the party leadership over its political strategy in Tamil Nadu and launched a new political movement, 'We The Leaders'. He said the movement would focus on "common man politics", challenge what he described as "cult and dynastic politics", and eventually evolve into a political party. He has outlined plans to contest the 2031 Tamil Nadu assembly elections.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed grows agitated with reporter after being pressed on family's alleged Muslim Brotherhood ties
articles.summary: Abdul El-Sayed clashed with an NBC reporter over his claim of no family ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, as his half-sister's posts say otherwise.
articles.body: Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed got into a tense exchange with a reporter on Wednesday as his claim about having no family connections to the Muslim Brotherhood draws scrutiny. On "NBC Nightly News," El-Sayed was pressed about social media posts made by his half-sister Eman Abdelhadi, alleging their mother was an active member of the Muslim Brotherhood in Egypt during the 1970s after he denied there were any family connections to the controversial Islamist group during an interview with NBC's Kristen Welker on Sunday's "Meet the Press." "Can you just explain it?" anchor Tom Llamas asked after reading some of Abdelhadi's posts. ABDUL EL-SAYED'S ALLEGED FAMILY TIES TO MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD SURFACE AFTER DENYING ANY LINK DURING NBC INTERVIEW "It's funny to me," El-Sayed responded. "I was born in 1984 down the street in Rochester Hills. I was raised here in Michigan, went to the University of Michigan, rebuilt the health department in this city, led the health department in this county — and you want to ask me about what's happening in Egypt in 1970? Are you serious?" "I get it, but you were asked a question, and you gave an answer," Llamas responded. "I have no ties, we have no ties," El-Sayed doubled down. EL-SAYED ASKED IF HE BELIEVES AMERICA IS 'READY FOR A MUSLIM PRESIDENT' AHEAD OF SENATE RACE The Democratic hopeful told Llamas he hadn't had conversations with his mother about her alleged Muslim Brotherhood activity and accused the anchor of using "hearsay evidence from a tweet." "That's just not serious," El-Sayed said. "But you've also gone after the president for truthfulness and when people ask you a question, do you expect the truth?" Llamas then asked. "Are you insinuating that somehow I was lying?" El-Sayed fired back. "I don't know, that's why I'm asking," Llamas responded. "And I'm telling you that I was not," El-Sayed told him. During an interview that aired on Sunday, Welker pressed El-Sayed whether he could "set the record straight" on allegations that he and his family had connections to the Muslim Brotherhood, to which he firmly replied, "No," before suggesting his Republican opponent, Mike Rogers, was floating Islamophobic attacks against him and his family. However, according to Abdelhadi, their mother was an active member of the Muslim Brotherhood. "Had an amazing talk with my mom about her activism in the Muslim Brotherhood during the early 70s while she was in college #respect," Abdelhadi wrote in a 2012 X post, as first reported by the Washington Free Beacon. EL-SAYED’S HALF SISTER OFFERED OCT 7 ‘BLESSING,’ ONE YEAR AFTER HAMAS ATTACK: ‘ALLAHU AKBAR’ Their mother, Fatten Elkomy, had attended Egypt's Alexandria University, which, according to a report from the Brookings Institution, had strong Muslim Brotherhood activity back in the 70s. In another 2012 post, Abdelhadi, a professor at the University of Chicago, wrote: "My family has long been MB, but I've always felt that it has navigated the political sphere poorly/destructively." In a third post from 2013, she wrote, "Praying for all my family that supports the #MB in #Egypt. Lie low, stay safe." CLICK HERE FOR THE LATEST MEDIA AND CULTURE NEWS An El-Sayed campaign spokesperson previously issued a statement to Fox News, saying, "Abdul is a dad and a doctor. He has spent his entire career working to keep Michiganders healthy and safe. Independent fact checkers have repeatedly debunked Mike’s lies, but their campaign continues to use bad faith attacks on Abdul's faith and family. Mike wants to distract from Trump’s agenda that is terrorizing Michigan families at the pump and at the grocery store." The campaign has also said the Muslim Brotherhood accusations have been "debunked as racist and untrue." Fox News Digital reached out to the El-Sayed campaign for additional comment. articles.title: China, Pakistan hold high-altitude army drills with Beijing-supplied arms
articles.summary: China and Pakistan launched their first joint army exercise in a high-altitude region of China's Xinjiang, with all weapons and military equipment used in
articles.body: China and Pakistan launched their first joint army exercise in a high-altitude region of China's Xinjiang, with all weapons and military equipment used in the drills supplied by Beijing, Chinese state media reported on Thursday.The exercise, named Karakoram 2026, began with an opening ceremony at a training base in Korla, in the Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region of northwestern China. The two countries have held annual joint air force and naval exercises, but this marks their first joint army training exercise, according to Chinese military officials.State-run CCTV reported that the drills involve several categories of Chinese military equipment, including Type 191 rifles, Type 201 squad machine guns, Type 11 armoured assault vehicles and Type 08 infantry fighting vehicles. Artillery systems, unmanned platforms and anti-drone systems have also been deployed.China is Pakistan's largest arms supplier, providing more than 80 per cent of the weapons supplied to the country's three armed services, according to the report.High-altitude drills highlight growing military cooperationThe deployment of Chinese equipment for high-altitude operations has drawn attention given China's military experience in the himalayan border region with India, according to the news agency PTI.Military affairs expert Wang Yunfei told the state-run Global Times that the use of medium-weight wheeled armoured vehicles in mountainous terrain reflected the operational considerations behind the exercise.According to Wang, wheeled armoured vehicles offer certain advantages over tracked platforms in high-altitude environments. They can move faster, particularly on roads, and are generally easier to maintain, making them suitable for transportation and combat missions across plateau terrain.He also noted that the use of Chinese equipment across multiple categories provided the participating forces with a relatively comprehensive combat system.The exercise demonstrates China's role in supplying military technology and equipment to Pakistan, Wang said. It could also help Islamabad assess the equipment for potential future purchases, further increasing the presence of Chinese-made systems in the Pakistan army.The drills therefore serve both as an opportunity for troops to familiarise themselves with the equipment and as preparation for closer operational cooperation.Wang added that the exercise reflected the high level of strategic trust between Beijing and Islamabad. Developing greater interoperability could support future joint activities involving counter-terrorism, border security and other military operations.Counter-terrorism operations form the core of the exerciseAccording to Chinese military officials, the exercise is focused on joint counter-terrorism operations and clearance missions in high-altitude areas.Senior Colonel Chen Xi, a spokesperson for China's ministry of National defence, said on Saturday that the programme would include training in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) operations, mobile target detection and firing, and long-range sniping.The exercise will also involve joint command activities and live-force training, according to the Chinese military.Military expert Zhang Jueshe told the global times that China and Pakistan had complementary capabilities in counter-terrorism, creating opportunities to deepen cooperation through intelligence sharing, joint operations, technology transfers and exchanges of operational experience.Zhang said China could provide Pakistan with technical assistance and equipment, including drones and intelligent combat platforms, to strengthen surveillance and early-warning capabilities against terrorist groups. Training and exchanges of counter-terrorism experience could also form part of the cooperation.At the same time, Pakistan's experience in managing complex border security challenges, dealing with local separatist groups and coordinating counter-terrorism operations could offer lessons for China in addressing similar non-traditional security threats, he added.Drills expected to strengthen China-Pakistan military tiesThe Karakoram 2026 exercise is expected to broaden military cooperation between the two countries, with a particular focus on counter-terrorism and high-altitude operations.Zhang said the drills would help strengthen mutual trust and improve coordination through the exchange of expertise and operational experience.The exercise also provides an opportunity for Chinese and Pakistani troops to practise working with common equipment and procedures, potentially improving their ability to operate together in future missions.The launch of the joint army drills marks a new phase in the two countries' military engagement, expanding cooperation beyond their established air force and naval exercises.You use AI every day. articles.title: Giant meat-eating crabs with crushing grip complicate Amelia Earhart expedition on remote island
articles.summary: The Purdue University expedition to find Amelia Earhart's Lockheed Electra has encountered massive coconut crabs while clearing trails on Nikumaroro Island.
articles.body: Massive meat-eating coconut crabs are posing an unusual challenge for the team searching for Amelia Earhart's missing plane on the remote Pacific island of Nikumaroro. Purdue University confirmed on Monday that the crew would sleep aboard its vessel rather than on the island, citing the enormous crustaceans as one reason for the decision. The 17-person expedition team arrived off Nikumaroro on Monday evening after a five-day voyage across the Pacific, going ashore the following morning to begin investigating clues that could help solve Earhart's disappearance. AMELIA EARHART MYSTERY ENTERS CRITICAL PHASE AS EXPLORERS ZERO IN ON MYSTERIOUS OBJECT "The crew will sleep nightly aboard the Marin Mainiku for a number of reasons, one of which is the presence of coconut crabs, whose size and overnight activity make staying on the island impractical," the university said. The team, which is 16 hours ahead of Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), has already encountered the massive crustaceans while working on the island. In a Tuesday statement, Purdue University officials said researchers came across at least four coconut crabs while clearing an overgrown trail to the island's lagoon. The path, nicknamed the "Gallagher Highway," had become heavily overgrown since the last expedition — forcing researchers and crew members to use machetes and hand chainsaws to clear a route. The work took about two hours. Despite the crab encounters, the animals "posed no threat to the operation," according to the university. DIVERS BRAVE DEADLY 'MOUNT EVEREST OF SHIPWRECKS' AS FAMED WRECK BREAKS APART The coconut crab is considered the largest terrestrial arthropod, according to a 2011 report from the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS). The crab digs shallow burrows for mating and molting and frequently maintains several burrows within its territory, the USGS report states. "The species is omnivorous and will scavenge carcasses, climb trees to access food or escape, and can live [for] over 40 years," added the USGS report. Coconut crabs are also equipped with two powerful pincers capable of cracking through the tough exterior of a coconut, according to London's Natural History Museum. NOAH'S ARK MYSTERY ENTERS NEW PHASE AS RESEARCHERS PROBE DEEP BENEATH SITE The crustaceans' claws have serrated edges that function like teeth, allowing them to break open the hard shells. "The squeeze of a coconut crab’s pincers can be much stronger than a human’s grip," the museum said. "There is a problem with coconut crabs and hermit crabs, but otherwise it’s a magical place." Researchers testing 29 wild coconut crabs found that their pincers could generate more than 1,765 newtons of force. "For comparison, humans have a maximum bite force of between 1,100 and 1,300 newtons," the museum added. One photo released by Purdue University shows expedition member Sirisha Bandla smiling as she holds a massive coconut crab, its long legs and claws extending outward. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Expedition member Renato LaRocca, who had previously visited Nikumaroro, acknowledged the challenges posed by the island's wildlife in an Oct. 9 university statement. "There is a problem with coconut crabs and hermit crabs, but otherwise it's a magical place," he said. Despite the challenges, Rick Pettigrew, executive director of the Archaeological Legacy Institute and leader of the expedition, said the team remained in "excellent spirits." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS "We continue to be well taken care of by our very capable Kiribati crew, and we are looking forward to the work ahead," he added. Purdue University told Fox News Digital on Thursday that the crabs have not caused any additional challenges for the crew. The expedition is investigating a mysterious anomaly detected in satellite imagery that some researchers believe could be Earhart's missing Lockheed Electra. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ The search is rooted in the Nikumaroro Hypothesis, which suggests Earhart's aircraft went down near the remote Pacific island. Earhart was just 39 years old when she disappeared on July 2, 1937, during her attempt to become the first woman to fly around the world. articles.title: India’s US ambassador blasts Jayapal’s statement on voter rolls purge
articles.summary: Vinay Mohan Kwatra, India’s ambassador to the U.S., said Rep. Pramila Jayapal’s (D-Wash.) remarks on the recent protests in India following a nationwide revision of voter lists are an “unacceptable interference in India’s internal affairs.” “India is a vibrant democracy, with robust, independent constitutional institutions and a longstanding record of free and fair elections,” Kwatra…
articles.body:
Vinay Mohan Kwatra, India’s ambassador to the U.S., said Rep. Pramila Jayapal’s (D-Wash.) remarks on the recent protests in India following a nationwide revision of voter lists are an “unacceptable interference in India’s internal affairs.”

“India is a vibrant democracy, with robust, independent constitutional institutions and a longstanding record of free and fair elections,” Kwatra wrote in a social platform X post Thursday. “Always open to constructive conversation with the Congresswoman to dispel her misconceptions.”

His post was in response to Jayapal’s post Wednesday on X , where she expressed concern over the Indian government’s decision to remove 130 million people from voting rolls.

“I am deeply concerned about the actions of the Indian government to purge 130 million people from the voting rolls,” Jayapal wrote in her post.

“This appears to be a similar playbook to what the Trump Administration is doing here at home to undermine voting rights in a democracy,” she added.

On Monday, opposition leaders and thousands of supporters marched to India’s Supreme Court in the nation’s capital, New Delhi, and submitted a petition to the chief justice alleging the irregularities in the nationwide revision of voter lists, which would remove more than 130 million voters from the list, The Associated Press reported .

The protests led by the “Cockroach” youth movement intensified, with thousands of activists being detained over the weekend in a crackdown across New Delhi, according to the AP report.

While critics say the revision of the voter lists is a politically motivated move that favors Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s party, the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Election Commission of India deny those allegations, saying this is a necessary step to remove duplicate and ineligible names, according to the AP report.

Earlier in the summer , the “Cockroach” movement sparked nationwide protests that lasted weeks leading to the resignation of the country’s education minister.

“Protecting democracies everywhere is essential work, and the Indian people — like the American people — deserve free and fair elections,” Jayapal added to her post. “Non-violent resistance movements are essential in these moments and I stand with the Indian people who are engaging in non-violent protests to counter anti-democratic efforts in India.”

The Hill has reached out to Jayapal’s office for comment.

John Healey has described the banks as part of "the crown jewels" of the UK economy, yet has refused to rule out a raid on the sector.

The biggest four banks collectively made around £15bn profit in the first six months of this year, leading to calls from trade unions and others for additional taxes.

However, the banking sector trade body, UK Finance, warned that "further increases in bank taxes would weaken competitiveness, discourage investment and job creation, and work against the government's ambition to deliver growth in every postcode".

The UK's biggest banks and building societies currently pay a surcharge of 3% on top of the baseline 25% rate of corporation tax, plus a levy on the assets held on their balance sheets.

The sector contributed nearly £40bn to the Treasury last year, if income tax on employees is factored in.

The bank levy generated £1.4bn last year and the surcharge a further £1.2bn.

There are a number of ways the chancellor could extract more money from the sector.

The 3% surcharge was reduced from 8% under Rishi Sunak, at the same time as he raised corporation tax from 19% to 25%. Returning the surcharge to its previous level could raise around £2bn a year.

The bank levy currently charges 0.1% on outstanding short-term loans and 0.05% on longer-dated loans, although mortgages are excluded from the calculation.

In the past banks have successfully argued that higher taxes would risk making the UK uncompetitive with other jurisdictions and would reduce their ability to lend, and therefore be anti-growth.

In truth, banks were pleasantly surprised they were not hit at the last Budget, given the large profits they have been making in recent years. Rising interest rates have expanded the margin between the rate at which they lend to customers and the rate they pay savers.

There is another option that has been discussed with Treasury officials. Currently banks can use losses from the past to offset against profits - thereby reducing their tax bill in any given year. Lloyds in particular has been a beneficiary of this policy, as large losses from the financial crisis have been used to lower tax bills ever since.

Some analysts and bank executives have pushed the idea of a moratorium on this practice for a few years, which would yield an estimated extra £1bn per year for the Treasury. That would provide a windfall while being "a lot more bearable", in the words of one bank executive.

It would also spare foreign banks from an additional hit, including JP Morgan, whose chief executive Jamie Dimon has warned that the UK already has one of the highest tax burdens on banks in the world. He warned that adding further sector-specific taxes could discourage investment and damage competitiveness.

However, industry leaders say any form of tax rise that hits UK banks and exempts foreign banks' operations in the UK would be hard to square with the government's push to back British business.

Whatever form it takes, banks believe the chancellor now has much more of an appetite to take a larger slice of their pie.

articles.title: ‘False accusations’: Maduro, wife rejects fresh torture allegations in New York court
articles.summary: Former Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro on Thursday dismissed new torture allegations against him and his wife, Cilia Flores, as “false accusations”
articles.body: Former Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro on Thursday dismissed new torture allegations against him and his wife, Cilia Flores, as “false accusations” during a court appearance in New York, where a judge entered not-guilty pleas on their behalf in a revised indictment accusing them of overseeing a state-sponsored campaign of repression.Maduro, who was brought to court in ankle shackles, criticised the indictment when judge Alvin K. Hellerstein asked him to enter a plea. He twice challenged the charges, saying they contained “false accusations and false testimony”. He spoke through an interpreter.Hellerstein entered a not-guilty plea on behalf of Maduro and Flores, who also denied the allegations. “I am completely innocent. I am not guilty,” she said through an interpreter when asked to enter her plea.The revised indictment accuses the couple of leading a system of repression in Venezuela that allegedly tortured scores of victims, including three Americans. Prosecutors claim the abuses included beatings, asphyxiation and electric shocks.According to the indictment, Maduro personally recommended torture methods, received updates on the treatment of specific victims and threatened to kill one prisoner's child as a form of psychological torture. Flores, a former attorney general, allegedly helped develop the repressive system and ordered the torture of specific individuals.Maduro's lawyer, Barry Pollack, said last week that the 63-year-old former president denied the charges and “looks forward to his day in court.”Trial date may be pushed backProsecutors told the judge that lawyers for both sides want the trial date moved from June 1 to June 14. The revised indictment expands the allegations against Maduro and Flores to cover alleged torture dating back to 2013, when Maduro succeeded his mentor, Hugo Chávez, as president.The couple were seized from their home in Caracas during a US military raid in January. They had earlier pleaded not guilty in a separate US drug trafficking case, which accuses them of conspiring to flood the United States with cocaine.Their lawyers have argued that the case should be dismissed on immunity grounds, saying Maduro was the leader of a foreign country and Flores was its first lady.Maduro faces years of scrutiny over alleged abusesMaduro was Venezuela's president from 2013 until his capture in January. He has been under investigation for years by the International Criminal Court over alleged crimes against humanity linked to his government's crackdown on political opponents. He has consistently denied wrongdoing.Torture is a crime under international law. It can be prosecuted outside the country where the abuse occurred, regardless of the victims' nationality.However, prosecuting foreign officials for torture in the United States is rare. Previous cases have included proceedings against the son of former Liberian president Charles Taylor, Russians accused of war crimes in Ukraine and a former prison warden in Syria under Bashar Assad's rule.You use AI every day. articles.title: From Tehran's pupils to missile makers: Why Houthis are a bigger threat now
articles.summary: Houthi rebels in Yemen are becoming less dependent on Iranian weapons after years of training and technical assistance from Tehran.
articles.body: Houthi rebels in Yemen are becoming less dependent on Iranian weapons after years of training and technical assistance from Tehran. This is allowing the group to assemble its own drones and missiles, posing a growing threat to Saudi Arabia as the US-Iran war strains regional air defences and depletes stocks of missile interceptors.The shift has become increasingly significant after Houthi attacks on Riyadh international airport and the headquarters of Saudi Aramco, the world's largest oil company, exposed vulnerabilities in Saudi Arabia's defences. Weapons and regional experts say the group's growing ability to produce its own weapons could make it harder to contain, even if Iranian supply routes are disrupted.Iran's strategy: Teach the Houthis to build weaponsIran has supplied weapons, money and training to the Houthis, formally known as Ansar Allah, for more than a decade. Tehran has denied arming the group in violation of a United Nations arms embargo.However, according to a report by news agency Reuters, Iran has also helped the Houthis develop the skills needed to assemble their own weapons. This includes drones and missiles made using dual-use components, which can serve both civilian and military purposes.Andreas Krieg, a senior security studies lecturer at King's College London, said Iran's Revolutionary Guards and members of the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah initially helped the Houthis understand missile systems and how to operate them."Former Yemeni military engineers and a growing generation of locally trained specialists have helped institutionalise these capabilities," he said."Tehran has not simply supplied the Houthis with weapons. It has helped create an indigenous military-industrial learning process that becomes progressively harder to dismantle, even if direct Iranian supply routes are disrupted."The strategy was designed to ensure that the Houthis could continue developing their military capabilities even if they lost access to direct Iranian supplies."The Revolutionary Guards were forward-looking. They looked at what happened if the Houthis couldn't receive equipment or weapons directly (from Iran), or if these were seized by US-allied forces," said Hamid Nikou, a former political advisor to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.Nikou said the strategy included teaching the Houthis how to assemble dual-use parts to make drones and even ballistic missiles."Iran has basically taught the Houthis how to fish," Nikou said.Iranian analysts say this has made the Houthis one of Tehran's most cost-effective and valuable military proxies.Chinese components add to Houthi capabilitiesThe Houthis are also diversifying their sources of weapons components, reducing their reliance on equipment supplied directly by Iran.Conflict Armament Research said in a report this week that the group was attempting to manufacture advanced medium-range ballistic missiles using components shipped from China. Yemen's internationally recognised government seized one such shipment."China has emerged as a particularly important commercial source, while Iran continues to provide specialised military technology, technical expertise and components that are difficult to obtain commercially," Krieg said.The development could complicate efforts to restrict the Houthis' weapons programme. Intercepting shipments and disrupting supply routes may not be enough if the group can obtain components through commercial channels and assemble weapons locally.The Houthis have also reportedly explored the use of artificial intelligence to improve their weapons.Anthropic said last month that "a cell of threat actors based in northern Yemen" had used its Claude AI assistant to help develop software for a guided rocket, a planned ballistic missile with a range of more than 2,000 km (1,240 miles) and a missile variant incorporating a hypersonic glide vehicle.These reported efforts point to the group's ambitions to expand its capabilities. They do not, by themselves, establish that all the weapons described have been successfully developed or deployed.US-Iran war puts Saudi air defences under pressureThe Houthis' expanding capabilities come as US allies in the Gulf face mounting pressure on their air defences.Since the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February, the United States has used large quantities of missile interceptors to protect its bases and allies, including Israel and Gulf countries. The depletion of these stocks has added to the challenges facing Saudi Arabia as it confronts the Houthi threat.Farzan Sabet, a Middle East expert at the Geneva Graduate Institute, said Saudi Arabia's air-defence network was not yet as sophisticated as those of Israel or Ukraine."Saudi Arabia, in terms of the sophistication of the military and the development of an integrated air defence network, is not really yet at the level of either Israel or Ukraine, and it just has a very tough job to do," he said.Saudi Arabia's size also makes it harder to defend against aerial attacks than Israel or a US military base, Sabet added.The latest attacks have raised concerns about the kingdom's ability to protect strategic infrastructure. They also threaten Saudi Arabia's efforts to attract foreign investment and diversify its economy beyond oil.Years of conflict have made the Houthis more capableThe Houthis' growing military capabilities reflect years of conflict and adaptation.The group has fought Saudi-backed forces in Yemen since 2014. The civil war settled into a fragile ceasefire in 2022.After Israel's assault on Gaza in 2023, which followed deadly Hamas-led attacks on Israel, the Houthis began firing rockets at Israel and targeting commercial shipping in the Red Sea.The subsequent US-Iran war reignited the conflict in Yemen, by which time the group had gained further operational experience and diversified its supply chains."They haven't been sitting still," Sabet said. "They were basically diversifying their supply chains... and as they gain operational experience, they're able to make those weapons more sophisticated."The Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis has said it intercepted several missiles fired at Saudi cities and destroyed 127 Houthi weapons storage facilities and launch platforms.Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki said the group had acquired advanced military technology with help from "regional actors". This included ballistic missiles, drones and fast boats carrying explosives.The growing challenge for Saudi Arabia and its allies is that disrupting weapons shipments or destroying launch sites may not be sufficient to neutralise a group that is learning to manufacture and improve its own weapons.You use AI every day. articles.title: Katie Price 'coached' ex's alleged rape victim, court told
articles.summary: Kieran Hayler says claims were fabricated amid the breakdown of his marriage.
articles.body:
Kieran Hayler has told jurors he thought his ex-wife Katie Price was "coaching" a 13-year-old girl he is accused of raping after discovering messages she sent to the alleged victim.

Hayler, 39, said he took photographs of messages on Price's phone in which she discussed claims that he fancied the girl and wrote: "I will make you a little star."

Hayler is on trial at Lewes Crown Court accused of three counts of rape and one count of sexual assault involving the teenager in West Sussex in 2016.

Giving evidence on Thursday, the former stripper denied the allegations and said: "I believe they've been fabricated."

He told the trial that "trust had gone on both sides" of his marriage to Price by mid-2013, and he admitted affairs with three other women during their relationship.

He told jurors "I am attracted to older women" and that all his significant relationships had been with older women.

Hayler said Price was also unfaithful during their relationship.

Asked by his defence barrister Arlette Piercy why he took pictures of the messages between Price and the complainant, he replied: "Because she made out that I fancied [the complainant].

He said he accessed her phone the same way she had accessed his, by using his fingerprint.

Asked about what this showed, he said: "The relationship is breaking down."

The court previously heard that Price messaged the teenager saying she had heard that Hayler and the girl had kissed and he had "tried it on" with her, adding later: "I will make you a little star."

Asked during her evidence about the phrase, Price said it was "a figure of speech".

On Thursday, Hayler said: "Everyone can interpret it how they want, it's very pushy. It's a very strange comment to make.

"I thought she was coaching her into [saying] something she shouldn't.

"I didn't send them anywhere, I took a picture on my phone."

He told the court he found the picture of the messages "recently" after taking his phones out of storage when moving home.

On Thursday, he also pleaded not guilty to four alternative counts of sexual activity with a child following the close of the prosecution case.

The charges were added to the indictment for the jury to consider as alternatives to the three rape counts and one count of sexual assault.

Judge Mark van der Zwart told jurors the prosecution alleged the complainant was raped, while Hayler's case was that nothing sexual had happened between them.

The court previously heard Hayler had claimed Price had "launched a campaign" against him after their marriage broke down and that the allegations formed part of it.

The couple were married at the time of the alleged offences before separating in 2018 and divorcing in 2021.

The complainant first contacted the NSPCC in 2021 and the charity referred her to police.

articles.title: 6,000 cops, 200 CAPF companies: As CJP pushes ahead with Tiranga march, Delhi prepares for a high-security friday
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Central Delhi is bracing for a massive security operation again on Friday, with the Delhi Police deploying around 6,000 personnel, supported by
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Central Delhi is bracing for a massive security operation again on Friday, with the Delhi Police deploying around 6,000 personnel, supported by 200 companies of the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) in shifts, ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) proposed ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ march at Connaught Place.From barricades and body-worn cameras to heavy security deployment and extensive traffic restrictions, the authorities are preparing for a high-security day in the heart of the national capital amid a standoff over the party’s proposed protest.The march, called by CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, is scheduled for 5pm on October 16 at Central Park in Connaught Place.The party has appealed to people to join the gathering carrying the national flag, describing it as a campaign to defend voting rights and the right to protest.Police personnel will be deployed at strategic locations, with barricades erected and the movement of protesters and commuters regulated to maintain law and order and prevent any untoward incident. The deployment of personnel in shifts is expected to ensure security throughout the day.However, the proposed gathering faces a major hurdle.The New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) has said Central Park will remain closed on Friday, while the Delhi Police said it may consider allowing a select group of people to gather at a suitable location to carry the national flag and sing the national anthem.A senior police officer said Jantar Mantar had also been denotified as a designated protest venue.Demonstrations can instead be held at Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground or CBD Ground after obtaining the requisite permission, the officer said.The proposed march follows the arrest of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who were sent to five days of judicial custody after entering Jantar Mantar and raising slogans demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The arrests came amid the continuing dispute over the withdrawal of Jantar Mantar’s status as a designated protest site.Possible traffic restrictions on 21 roadsThe heightened security arrangements are also expected to affect traffic across central Delhi.In a specific advisory issued ahead of the proposed gathering, the Delhi Traffic Police said movement on several roads in and around Connaught Place could be affected from 3pm.The police said dynamic traffic diversions may be implemented depending on the prevailing situation.The roads and stretches likely to be affected are:Sansad MargBaba Kharak Singh MargShaheed Bhagat Singh MargPanchkuian RoadBasant LaneChelmsford RoadMinto RoadBarakhamba RoadKasturba Gandhi MargJanpathRail BhawanRafi MargC-HexagonMandi HousePatel ChowkWindsor PlaceGole Dak KhanaAshok Road (from GPO to C-Hexagon)Tilak MargTolstoy MargSikandra RoadThe traffic police has advised commuters to plan their journeys in advance, allow sufficient additional travel time and use public transport wherever possible.Motorists have also been asked to follow the directions of traffic personnel and avoid roadside parking, using designated parking facilities instead.Commuters can access real-time updates, traffic alerts and information on alternate routes through the Delhi Traffic Police website and its official social media handles, including @dtptraffic on X, Instagram and Facebook.For assistance, they can call the traffic helplines at 1095 or 011-25844444.CJP intensifies campaignThe proposed march marks another escalation in the CJP’s campaign against Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.At a joint press conference in Delhi on Thursday, Dipke appealed to political parties, student organisations and civil society groups to join the protest, urging them to set aside ideological differences."I request all political parties and civil society groups to rise above ideology and come together. If the right to vote is not saved, democracy will not be saved," Dipke said.The CJP has alleged large-scale deletions from electoral rolls and accused the authorities of failing to address its concerns. These remain allegations made by the party.The campaign began in Mumbai on October 2 before moving to Delhi. Planned demonstrations and attempts to reach Jantar Mantar subsequently led to multiple detentions.The party announced the Connaught Place march after continuing to press for permission to protest at Jantar Mantar.With Central Park scheduled to remain closed, Connaught Place not recognised as an authorised protest venue and traffic restrictions expected from the afternoon, Friday’s gathering is set to test the Delhi Police’s crowd-management arrangements across the heart of the capital.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Trump ramps up third-country US deportations despite global rights outcry
articles.summary: Official data shows tens of thousands of migrants and asylum seekers have been sent to countries they have no ties to.
articles.body:
United States immigration authorities have dramatically stepped up detentions and deportations since January 2025, when Donald Trump became president.

Trump campaigned on a pledge to implement the “largest deportation operation in American history”. Officers with the Department of Homeland Security, the agency tasked with the crackdown, now make thousands of arrests a day across the country.

That includes people who are seeking asylum in the US, who are supposed to be given a chance to explain dangers they might face in their home country. And US law and international treaties, like the United Nations Convention Against Torture, prohibit authorities from deporting someone to any country in which they will be persecuted or tortured.

Many of those being detained in the US immigration crackdown say they are at risk of being hurt or killed if they return to their native countries, so the Trump administration has looked for alternative places to deport them, including places someone might have no cultural or legal ties to.

Third-country deportations, as the practice is known, have been criticised by the US as well as global rights groups like Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch, as well as the UN.

Critics of the practice say some of the countries taking in the deportees have a record of human rights abuses themselves, or are so dangerous that the US government tells its own citizens not to travel there. They also say there is little to ensure these third countries will give deportees a fair hearing on their cases for asylum, and in the end might send them back to their native countries to face persecution there.

Third-country deportations are not new, but rights groups say they were extremely rare before the Trump administration, and have never been used by the US at the scale they are now. Those being sent to other countries, rights groups say, would not have been deported without their consent. Some US courts have said the practice is illegal, but the US Supreme Court has allowed it to continue, including in a ruling in September.

Experts at the UN have said the practice was leading to a “cascade of human rights violations” across the globe, threatening to undo norms around how refugees and asylum seekers are treated.

A closer look at the third-country deportations

Rights groups have tried to tally forcible third-country deportations, and according to the nonprofits Refugees International and Human Rights First, more than 25,000 people have been subject to forcible third-country deportations so far, based on media reports and information from attorneys.

The Department of Homeland Security’s own data includes more than 16,000 cases of third-country deportations since Trump came into office in January 2025 and August 2026, the latest month for which data is available. The data, provided to the Deportation Data Project based at the University of California, Berkeley and the University of California, Los Angeles and analysed by Al Jazeera, is likely an undercount.

Deportations to these countries need the approval of authorities there, so the Trump administration has sought to make agreements, or reach informal understandings on how to send deportees to a growing list of countries.

Some countries have agreed to keep deportees in prisons, like El Salvador and Eswatini .

Others have agreed to hold deportees temporarily, with some signing Asylum Cooperative Agreements with the US, or “Safe Third Country Agreements”, which allow deportees to pursue asylum claims in a third country that has agreed to host them.

According to rights groups Refugees International and Human Rights First, many of those deported have no idea where they are being sent, and end up finding themselves in countries where they do not speak the language and have little cultural understanding. Some don’t even have any documents like passports or identification cards, making it difficult to live there.

The list of countries people are being deported to has grown as the US offers financial aid, or business or visa concessions, in exchange for countries taking in third-country nationals the Trump administration wants to remove.

Liberia has agreed to take up to 1,200 deportees, for instance. The Trump administration at one point said it would extend the validity of certain visas for Liberians from 12 to 36 months, and has committed $124m for the country’s health services.

In Cameroon, which agreed to take third-country nationals from the US in December 2025, the Trump administration has pledged to give $30m for the UN’s refugee work there, and $400m over the coming years for the country’s health services.
