articles.title: Malnutrition stalks the most vulnerable in Afghanistan as aid cuts leave millions helpless
articles.summary: KABUL, Afghanistan — Lying in her hospital cot, the 3-year-old girl roamed the room with her gray-green eyes, but her body was listless.
articles.body: KABUL, Afghanistan — Lying in her hospital cot, the 3-year-old girl roamed the room with her gray-green eyes, but her body was listless. Her mother sat by her bedside, quietly weeping. Just a few months ago, she lost her 5-year-old daughter, Khadija, to the same condition: malnutrition. Both girls had the same symptoms: thin limbs but swollen hands, feet and belly, signs of a severe type of malnutrition caused by protein deficiency. And now 25-year-old Malika is terrified that Kalsoum, her youngest daughter, will meet the same fate as Khadija. “I am worried about her, that she might die,” Malika said, wiping her tears with her green headscarf. “My husband is a day laborer. Sometimes there is work, sometimes there isn’t.” The $3-$4.60 he earns on days when he can find work just isn’t enough to feed the family, which also includes three young boys. Kalsoum is far from alone. In the malnutrition ward in the Indira Gandhi Institute of Child Health, Afghanistan’s main children’s hospital, all 20 beds — the maximum the hospital can afford — are full. Across Afghanistan, hunger and malnutrition are rising dramatically. Unprecedented levels “More people are suffering from hunger than ever before,” John Aylieff, Afghanistan country director for the World Food Program, told The Associated Press. He said 19 million people — nearly 40% of the population — would be facing acute hunger, “the life-threatening type of hunger,” in the next few months. Even more worrying is that acute malnutrition, which kills if left untreated, is spiraling. “Acute malnutrition is at unprecedented levels already,” Aylieff said. “In the next year 5.3 million women and children in this country will need treatment for acute malnutrition, the type of malnutrition which if not treated leads rather precipitously to to death.” That is 1.3 million more than in 2022, Aylieff said, when Afghanistan’s economy teetered on the brink of collapse after the U.S.-led coalition’s withdrawal and the Taliban’s seizure of power. The vast majority are children, according to data in the latest Integrated Food Security Phase Classification issued Thursday. Children, whose bodies are still developing and therefore have higher nutritional needs, are most at risk when food runs scarce. Overlapping crises are contributing to spiraling hunger Afghanistan, one of the world’s poorest countries, has been buffeted by a myriad of overlapping crises in recent years. The legacy of four decades of war is compounded by a yearlong closure of border crossings with Pakistan due to a simmering conflict, depriving Afghanistan of its main trade route. Added to that is the forcible return since 2023 of more than 5 million Afghan refugees from neighboring Iran and Pakistan who are putting pressure on limited resources; natural disasters such as drought, floods and earthquakes; and the crisis in the Middle East. Poverty is the main driving force behind the hunger crisis, with millions simply unable to afford nutritious food. With the crisis in the Middle East impacting economies across the world, Afghanistan has not been immune. “The price of food has gone up by between 10 and 30% for the basic staple commodities, the commodities that the poor eat. So the poor are being priced out of the market,” Aylieff said. But one of the most significant factors has been the sharp decline in international aid on which Afghanistan has long relied. The Taliban takeover in 2021 saw direct foreign aid halted almost overnight, driving millions into poverty and hunger. Women and children turned away Funding cuts to humanitarian organizations, including the halting of U.S. aid to programs such as the WFP’s food distribution, have severed a lifeline for millions. The U.N.’s food agency is the largest provider of food assistance in Afghanistan but has just 12% of the funding it had in 2022, Aylieff said. “We are forced to turn away six out of seven acutely malnourished women and children from those health clinics because we simply do not have the food to give them to save their child’s life,” Aylieff said. “That is, in my view, an international scandal. … And the very bleak challenge is that too many members of the international community are woefully indifferent to the suffering of Afghan children.” Pleading for funding The Indira Gandhi hospital’s malnutrition ward is almost always at capacity now. Sometimes, it has more patients than beds, and two children will share a cot, said Dr. Mohammad Arif Hassanzai, head of the hospital’s internal medicine department. “The number of patients with lower-grade malnutrition is extremely high, yet our current capacity limits us to admitting only the severe cases to these 20 beds,” Hassanzai said. “The assistance we receive from donors covers only this specific capacity, but if more resources were available, we could potentially accommodate 60, 70 or even up to 100 patients.” The funding cuts both pain and anger Hassanzai. “I am deeply concerned about why this health assistance has been reduced,” he said. “Must the politics unfolding in Afghanistan inevitably impact patients, causing them to suffer from malnutrition and even die? Healthcare should always remain separate from politics. … I must ask, as a doctor: why has this aid been cut off?” Hunger at home A few floors up from his office in the malnutrition ward, 25-year-old Zarmina cradles her daughter, Fatma, whose forehead is covered with white surgical tape holding a nasal feeding tube in place. At 2 years old, Fatma weighs just 4.8 kilograms (10.5 pounds), about half of what is considered healthy. Zarmina, whose husband is a day laborer from Logar province, says Fatma was initially admitted to a hospital in Logar, along with three of her other four children. All were malnourished. But Fatma’s condition was so serious she was referred to the hospital in Kabul. Her family had to borrow money to fund the trip. Twelve days after she was admitted, Fatma is still struggling to gain weight. Zarmina isn’t sure how long she will have to say in Kabul. “I am here, and I am also worried about my other children,” she says. Her other daughters have been discharged from the hospital in Logar and are being cared for by relatives. But the family is still desperately poor, and she doesn’t know how they will be able to eat. In other times, aid organizations might have been able to step in. But the funding cuts mean more and more families like Zarmina’s are left helpless. “The humanitarian crisis in Afghanistan is not so much being defined by what humanitarians can do, but actually by what we cannot do,” Aylieff said. “Because funding cuts are preventing us from mounting the response that we need.”

articles.title: Michigan woman Kimberly Kemper seeks $250 refund after $350 deep clean, alleging dirty dishes, untouched walls and baseboards; cleaner offered $100 and allegedly failed to return for a promised re-clean
articles.summary: A Michigan woman has taken to social media to share her experience with a cleaning service after allegedly paying $350 for a deep clean, only to find
articles.body: A Michigan woman has taken to social media to share her experience with a cleaning service after allegedly paying $350 for a deep clean, only to find parts of her home still dirty. Kimberly Kemper claimed she had to rewash dishes, clean her floors herself and even climb into a dumpster to retrieve her sink strainer after the appointment.In an October 13 Facebook post, Kemper shared photographs and messages relating to her experience with Cecilia’s Cozy Cleaning. She alleged that several areas of her home, including walls, baseboards and stairs, had been left untouched, while dishes had been put away without being properly cleaned.When Kemper contacted the business owner, Cecilia Bodart, to raise her concerns, Bodart offered to return and address the issues. However, Kemper said the promised follow-up visit never happened, leading to a dispute over how much of the $350 payment should be refunded.Homeowner says walls and baseboards were left uncleanedKemper said Bodart had visited her home before providing a quote. They discussed cleaning the kitchen, living room, bathroom, hallway and stairs, while the bedrooms were excluded from the job.According to Kemper, she specifically highlighted the walls the night before the scheduled cleaning. In a message to Bodart, she wrote, “I'm so excited for these walls to be clean.” Bodart responded, “I got you!!”Kemper said she trusted Bodart because their children attended the same school. She also said she paid for the service before inspecting the house.However, after checking the property, Kemper claimed that sections of the walls she had expected to be cleaned remained untouched. She also alleged that cabinets were still dirty above eye level and that parts of the baseboards and other surfaces had been overlooked.To support her complaint, Kemper posted photographs of cleaning rags she said she had used to wipe down areas after the service.Questioning what had been completed for the $350 fee, Kemper messaged Bodart: “Can you tell me what work did get done so I can justify it?” She added, “This is a genuine ask.”Cleaner offers to return, but homeowner says nobody showed upIn response to the complaint, Bodart described Kemper as a client who “wasn't completely satisfied with her cleaning” and said that “everyone has different expectations.”In their private messages, Bodart listed walls, baseboards, windowsills and cabinets among the areas she said had been cleaned. She maintained that she and an employee had performed work that warranted payment, even as she acknowledged that Kemper was unhappy with the result.Bodart subsequently offered to return to correct the cleaning and provide a free routine cleaning visit afterward. Kemper said she could not accommodate the same-day offer but agreed to a Tuesday appointment after Bodart suggested the day, noting that her family would be home.However, Kemper said she was still waiting for confirmation on Tuesday morning. Kemper said she had not been told in advance that another worker would be entering the property.Bodart later apologised for not informing her about the additional worker.Cleaning experts recommend clarifying what a service includesThe scope of a deep clean can vary between providers. The cleaning trade association ISSA recommends that customers ask for a detailed list of included tasks when obtaining an estimate and clarify whether the business offers a satisfaction guarantee.ISSA also advises customers to establish whether an individual cleaner or a team will visit, ask how workers are screened and request advance notice of changes to the cleaning crew when that is important to them.The dispute also drew attention to the challenges customers can face when expectations about a paid service are not clearly agreed upon or when follow-up communication breaks down.Homeowner asks people not to harass business ownerAs the complaint circulated online, Bodart reportedly received unwanted messages from people outside the dispute. articles.summary: Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-Pa.) called Ukraine’s loss of access to Starshield, the military version of Starlink internet, a “major problem” and said Congress would respond if the U.S. abandons its support for Ukraine. Ukraine said it was suddenly unable to use Starshield on Wednesday, which could have major impacts on its defense operations and ability…
articles.body:
Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-Pa.) called Ukraine’s loss of access to Starshield, the military version of Starlink internet, a “major problem” and said Congress would respond if the U.S. abandons its support for Ukraine.

Ukraine said it was suddenly unable to use Starshield on Wednesday, which could have major impacts on its defense operations and ability to stop Russian attacks. Multiple outlets had reported the U.S. threatened to cut off intelligence and weapons support to Ukraine prior to the outage.

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, who owns Starlink, clarified in a post to the social platform X that Starshield is managed by the U.S. government and any limits on the service would be decided on by President Trump or the military.

Fitzpatrick threatened “consequences” if the U.S. “goes dark” on Ukraine, telling The Wall Street Journal that Congress could halt funding for federal agencies responsible.

“Agencies won’t get funding if they’re not doing their jobs,” he told the Journal.

Fitzpatrick, who represents Pennsylvania’s 1st Congressional District, is one of just a handful of Republicans in the House defending a seat won by former Vice President Kamala Harris in 2024. He faces a tough reelection battle, though he has overperformed other Republicans in the past.

The Starshield incident comes amid growing criticism from Democrats and some Republicans over Trump’s wavering support for Ukraine. Trump said he struck a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to purchase Russian diesel, potentially giving Russia a financial lifeline to continue its war effort. Trump has also called for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to be replaced and blamed high gas prices on Ukraine attacking Russian refineries, not on the U.S. war with Iran.

Trump’s latest moves on Ukraine have prompted multiple Republican members of Congress to speak out.

Rep. Don Bacon (R-Neb.), who is retiring at the end of the term, said Congress will not advance Trump’s agenda if he abandons Ukraine.

“Their agenda is dead unless they change paths,” Bacon wrote on X.

Another retiring Republican and frequent Trump critic, North Carolina Sen. Thom Tillis, said Trump’s Russian oil deal is “tarnishing” the efforts of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-S.C.), a prominent Ukraine supporter.

Zelensky told ABC News on Sunday that Trump is attacking him because he cannot stop Putin.

“These people can’t find a key how to stop Putin,” Zelensky said. “It’s more simple to speak about the prices and connect it with Ukraine.”

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV’s doctors say X-ray ‘showed good recovery’ after lung surgery: Vatican
articles.summary: “He carried out his daily activities independently. His physiotherapy session included a full range of physical activities,” doctors added.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — The Vatican provided encouraging news from Pope Leo XIV’s doctors about his recovery after he underwent surgery earlier this week to remove part of his right lung and was diagnosed with cancer.

On the 71-year-old American pope’s third day in the hospital, he “underwent routine checks,” including a chest X-ray that “showed good recovery of the lung that underwent surgery,” the pope’s doctors said in a statement from the Vatican’s press office.

“He carried out his daily activities independently. His physiotherapy session included a full range of physical activities,” doctors added. “Overall, his postoperative recovery is progressing normally.”

Leo had surgery Tuesday afternoon to remove what he called a “small, localized nodule” from his lung. Following the operation, doctors confirmed that Leo has a common type of lung cancer called lung adenocarcinoma “as suspected from the preoperative examinations.”

At the time of this reporting, the Vatican hasn’t announced any changes to Leo’s previously announced one-week hospitalization.

NewsNation’s Josie Fischels contributed to this report.

articles.title: Ethiopian forces expand control in Tigray as militia claims Eritrean losses
articles.summary: Eritrea denies troop movement inside northern Ethiopia as US calls for de-escalation.
articles.body:
Ethiopian forces and allied fighters say they have expanded control across Tigray and entered the historic city of Aksum, as fighting in the northern region continues.

The pro-government militia, the Tigray Peace Force (TPF), also claimed on Thursday that troops from neighbouring Eritrea have retreated towards the border.

Solomon Hailemariam, spokesperson for the TPF, said Eritrean forces had sustained significant casualties during the fighting.

But Eritrea’s Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel rejected the claims as false in comments to local media. The extent of the reported losses could not be independently verified.

The Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project (ACLED), an independent conflict-monitoring organisation, documented Ethiopian government forces and TPF fighters entering Aksum, while rival Tigrayan fighters remained in surrounding mountainous areas.

ACLED also reported Eritrean troops withdrawing across the border through Zalambessa, following advances by Ethiopian forces and their allies into several strategic towns.

“Ethiopian troops are on one side, and Eritrean troops are on the other,” Selam, a resident of Zalambessa whose first name was changed for security reasons, told the AFP news agency on Thursday.

AFP reported that there is no fighting now, but the town has been without power or water for a week.

“We are caught in the middle and living in deep anxiety,” Salem told the news agency.

ACLED also documented Ethiopian tanks and heavy weapons moving towards the Eritrean border on Tuesday, raising concerns about a possible confrontation between the neighbouring countries.

Addis Ababa has accused Eritrea, as well as Sudan and Egypt, of backing a rebel alliance of seven groups that is fighting the government of Abiy Ahmed.

Eritrea has denied accusations that its forces entered Tigray to support the armed opposition groups, accusing Ethiopia of threatening its sovereignty.

Eritrea, which fought alongside Ethiopia’s federal army in the 2020-2022 war, severed diplomatic ties with Ethiopia over the accusations earlier this month.

Khartoum and Cairo have also denied involvement in the conflict.

The TPF supports Ethiopia’s federal government in its campaign against the Tigrayan rebels linked to the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF).

Ethiopian forces captured Tigray’s regional capital Mekelle earlier this month, and the TPLF confirmed that it had withdrawn from the city and moved its regional administration “temporarily” to another location. Government forces also retook the towns of Adwa and Adigrat from the TPLF without a fight. Further, there are reports of Ethiopian advances in the town of Rama, close to the border with Eritrea.

On Wednesday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called for de-escalation in a phone call with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy, following reports of the alleged confrontation between Ethiopian and Eritrean forces.

Rubio said the region could not tolerate more conflict, according to a statement from the US Department of State.

articles.title: Dying in ICE custody: Inside one family’s story of heartbreak
articles.summary: Ismael Ayala-Uribe was one of 53 people to die in ICE custody during Trump’s first 500 days back in office.
articles.body:
Los Angeles, California – Saturdays marked a weekly pilgrimage for Lucia Uribe. Every weekend, she would travel to the edge of California's desert to visit her son, Ismael Ayala-Uribe, in detention.

Ismael was among the hundreds of thousands of people swept up in United States President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown.

Born in Mexico and brought to the US as a child, he was arrested on August 17 while working at a car wash. Ever since, he had been in the custody of immigration authorities, first at a local jail and later at a detention centre for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in Adelanto, California.

But one Saturday was different. Lucia remembers that Ismael’s hands looked paler, his eyes were bloodshot, and the fever he had was rising.

“Mom, I’m not going to make it,” Lucia recalls Ismael telling her. There was little she could do but reassure him.

“I told him, ‘Oh, my son, just hang in there as long as you can,’” Lucia said. “When I said goodbye to him, I felt something in my chest, a tightness, and it made me want to cry.”

It was the last time she would see her son alive. Lucia’s fears were confirmed by a knock at her door two days later, when police told her that her son had died at 2:32am on September 22, 2025.

Ismael was one of more than 50 people to die in ICE custody during the first 500 days of Trump's second term.

A coroner's report from the San Bernardino County Sheriff's Department in southern California found that his death was caused by complications from an abscess in his pelvic region.

Ismael's family, however, has argued that insufficient medical treatment in ICE facilities led a preventable infection to fester into a deadly condition.

For months, the Al Jazeera documentary series Fault Lines has spoken to people in ICE custody and the families of those who never made it out alive, to understand the conditions that could have led to deaths like Ismael's.

What it found was that 2025, the year Ismael died, was the deadliest year in history for those in ICE custody. But experts fear 2026 is on track to match or surpass that record.

articles.title: A Kansas couple wanted a beach without leaving home, so they turned two acres of their Olathe backyard into a 100,000-gallon lagoon with six waterfalls, tropical fish and a 23,000-pound boulder
articles.summary: A Kansas couple who wanted a tropical getaway without moving away from their family turned two acres of their Olathe backyard into a huge 100,000-gallon
articles.body: A Kansas couple who wanted a tropical getaway without moving away from their family turned two acres of their Olathe backyard into a huge 100,000-gallon swimming lagoon. Homeowners Melissa and Mike Morris spent nearly a year building their private outdoor retreat. The lagoon stretches about 100 feet long and 50 feet wide on their ten-acre property. It features six cascading waterfalls, tropical fish trained to respond to human voices, and thousands of pounds of imported granite rocks, including one giant boulder weighing 23,000 pounds. In an interview with Kansas City Homes & Style magazine, Melissa Morris described how their suburban backyard had changed. "I look out the window, and I get this fat, cheesy grin on my face," Morris told Kansas City Homes & Style. "I'm like, is this real? Do I actually live here? Even when I'm slaving and sweating in it, I look around, and I smile, because I realize this is paradise."Inspired by a trip to TahitiThe project grew from the couple's wish to enjoy a coastal lifestyle while staying close to their family in Kansas. Traditional swimming pools in the Midwest can face long-term damage from harsh winter weather. Repeated freezing and thawing can crack concrete and damage paving. After watching relatives deal with expensive repairs to a traditional pool, Morris wanted a natural swimming area that could better handle the local climate. The idea for the lagoon took shape during a holiday in Tahiti. The couple stayed at a resort with a natural stone cove protected by a reef-like structure. Warm water and tropical reef fish could move freely through the Tahitian cove, while larger ocean animals were kept out. Natural stepping stones around the water added to the unusual swimming experience. Morris returned to Olathe determined to create a similar ocean-like setting at home. She imagined a natural swimming pond with beach-style entrances instead of the usual walls and chlorinated water of a standard pool.Hauling massive boulders from ColoradoThe lagoon's main visual feature is its large stone structure. It uses granite boulders brought from high-altitude areas of Colorado rather than locally available Kansas limestone. According to a feature published by Kansas City Homes & Style, Morris asked a friend to travel to Colorado and climb to heights of 14,000 feet to choose specific granite rocks. She wanted stones with gray and white streaks and sparkling mineral patterns. To make sure construction workers did not accidentally install her favourite stones with their best sides facing down, Morris marked important rocks with red spray-painted dots. The largest rock on the property arrived by chance when a delivery crew loaded an oversized 23,000-pound boulder onto its truck. The enormous stone needed an excavator to slide it off the vehicle. Once the crew stood the boulder upright, the couple noticed its unusual face-like shape. They quickly named it "Jabba the Hutt," after the fictional Star Wars character.Creating a year-round tropical landscapeTo make the lagoon feel like a real beach, the couple added two zero-entry shorelines. These gently slope into the water and are made from smooth, tumbled white marble rather than ordinary sand. This helps prevent loose grit from getting into the water filters. The water ranges from a shallow five-foot shelf to six and a half feet in the central diving area. Water moves continuously through a filtration system designed by Aquascape. The couple hired local company Good Earth Water Gardens to build the main lagoon and its large stone barriers. The surrounding garden includes artificial palm trees made with real palm husks. They give the area a tropical look while allowing it to withstand freezing Kansas winters. The couple also added natural wood features, including a hollowed-out walnut log recovered from a river on Mike Morris's family property. "Mike and I are both pretty ambitious and planned on doing it ourselves, but after almost finishing the waterfall pond by our barn, we realized this lagoon would probably take us two years to complete on our own and I don't have that much patience or time," Morris explained to Kansas City Homes & Style. The couple also put in 12 to 14 hours a day working on the surrounding gardens, cabana structures, and outdoor seating areas.Sharing the private lagoonThe finished backyard project, officially named "Morris Lagoon," has attracted attention from well beyond the local community. After videos of the 100,000-gallon lagoon spread across social media platforms, the couple began receiving requests from photographers who wanted to arrange private photo sessions on the property. Morris has not ruled out hosting small private gatherings or weddings there in the future. For now, however, the couple is focused on finishing the last landscaping details and enjoying their own private retreat.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 5 GOP House members join letter urging Trump to cancel Russia diesel deal, up sanctions
articles.summary: Five House Republicans signed on to a letter Thursday urging President Trump to cancel the Russian diesel deal he announced last week. GOP Reps. Don Bacon (Neb.), Brian Fitzpatrick (Pa.), Michael McCaul (Texas), Dan Newhouse (Wash.) and Joe Wilson (S.C.) joined 17 of their Democratic colleagues in writing they were “particularly concerned” about the deal.…
articles.body:
Five House Republicans signed on to a letter Thursday urging President Trump to cancel the Russian diesel deal he announced last week.

GOP Reps. Don Bacon (Neb.), Brian Fitzpatrick (Pa.), Michael McCaul (Texas), Dan Newhouse (Wash.) and Joe Wilson (S.C.) joined 17 of their Democratic colleagues in writing they were “particularly concerned” about the deal .

Trump said Russia agreed to “immediately” supply 300,000 tons of diesel to the global marketplace, with another 500,000 tons on the way in November.

Under the agreement , Russia would supply another 4 million tons after November if its refineries are capable of doing so amid attacks by Ukraine , the president added.

In conjunction with Trump’s announcement, the Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued a waiver authorizing Russian producers to import diesel fuel into the U.S. The waiver is effective through April 6, 2027.

The bipartisan group of lawmakers pressed Trump to reconsider and copied Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Secretary of State Marco Rubio on the letter.

“We urge the Administration to revoke this license and not issue further general licenses that reopen Russian energy transactions and restore revenue to the Kremlin’s war chest,” they wrote.

The lawmakers also asked Trump to explain how he can “reconcile” the Treasury Department’s license with an existing ban on Russian energy imports to the U.S.

A spokesperson for the Treasury Department referred The Hill to the department’s Office of Terrorism and Financial Intelligence writing on social platform X last week that the license “is consistent with similar actions previously taken” by the OFAC and “is in compliance with all applicable laws.”

The Hill has also reached out to the White House and State Department for comment.

McCaul, the former chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said in a statement that he understands Trump’s “desire to bring down diesel prices,” which remain above $6 per gallon amid the Iran war .

But the outgoing lawmaker added he was “concerned” the diesel deal “will only fuel the Kremlin’s violence and destruction,” noting Russian forces have attacked Ukrainian energy infrastructure sites this week — after Trump said the two sides agreed to an “ energy ceasefire .”

In the letter, the Republicans also encouraged the president to forcefully apply legislation aimed at boosting sanctions on Russia.

The law, named for the late Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-S.C.), passed the Senate and House with strong bipartisan majorities in September.

“Designations should reach the officials, oligarchs, banks, and state enterprises directing and financing the war, as well as the foreign banks, shadow fleet operators, and intermediaries that help Russia evade restrictions,” the lawmakers wrote three days before a deadline for Trump to set secondary tariffs on countries that import Russian products and designate Russian entities for sanctions.

“We stand ready to work with your Administration to ensure this law achieves the purpose for which Congress enacted it,” the letter concluded.

articles.title: FSDA cancels licences of 14 medicine firms in Aminabad
articles.summary: FSDA cancels licences of 14 Aminabad medicine firms and suspends 29 in Lucknow crackdown on fake medicines; Rs 41.58 lakh seized, 9 FIRs filed.
articles.body: Lucknow: In a crackdown on fake medicines, Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) cancelled the drug licences of 14 establishments and suspended those of 29 firms in Aminabad’s medicine market.An FSDA official said the establishments whose licences were cancelled had been found involved in cross-billing and the trade in fake medicines. Deficiencies in the operations of some firms led to the suspension of their licences.An FSDA investigation conducted in August revealed that some firms were recording purchases and sales on paper while circulating fake and counterfeit medicines in the market.On Aug 12, nine FIRs were registered at Aminabad police station against these firms under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). In July, the official added, fake medicines were seized from illegal warehouses in Alambagh, Bakshi Ka Talab and Aminabad in Lucknow. An FIR was also registered against eight firms in Aminabad and a software vendor on charges of fake billing and software tampering.A cross-billing syndicate operating without the physical supply of medicines was also detected in Kaiserbagh. Illegal medicines worth approximately Rs 41.58 lakh have been seized in Lucknow so far. articles.title: Northern Ireland ex-DUP leader Donaldson sentenced to 15 years for child sex crimes
articles.summary: Judge says Jeffrey Donaldson never apologised to victims as politician seeks to appeal his convictions.
articles.body:
The former leader of Northern Ireland’s largest unionist party has been sentenced to 15 years in jail for child ⁠⁠sex offences.

Jeffrey Donaldson, who led the Democratic Unionist Party (DUP), stared straight ahead as Judge Paul Ramsey handed down the 63-year-old’s sentence on Thursday.

Ramsey described the case as “disturbing and disquieting”, ‌‌assessing Donaldson as having a medium chance of reoffending. He described the politician’s fall as “a catastrophic descent into disgrace”.

Donaldson has been in prison awaiting sentence since June after he was convicted of one count of rape, 13 counts of indecent assault and four counts of gross indecency against two girls between ⁠⁠1985 and 2008.

He denied all the charges and is seeking to appeal against his convictions.

The case is one of the highest-profile cases in the British-run region in recent times.

Donaldson was one of Northern Ireland’s best-known politicians and its longest-serving lawmaker in the British Parliament when he was arrested and charged in March 2024.

He immediately resigned as the leader of the DUP after he was charged with what he called “allegations of an historic nature”.

Prosecutor Rosemary Walsh told a pre-sentencing hearing last month that one of the victims described the abuse as “the worst moment of her life”.

The other victim said her childhood had been stolen and that she had carried around feelings of “shame” ever since. The victims, neither of whom can be identified for legal reasons, gave evidence during ⁠⁠the trial.

Judge Ramsey said Donaldson had doubled down on his denials and not offered one word of an apology or expressed shame.

Donaldson will likely spend seven-and-a-half years in prison as he qualifies for an automatic remission of his sentence, the Lady Chief Justice’s Office of ⁠⁠Northern Ireland said. This is because the offences were committed before a change in the law allowing a judge to choose what portion of a sentence is spent in custody.

In 2021, Donaldson became leader of the DUP, the party founded by Protestant cleric Ian Paisley at the height of three decades of sectarian bloodshed, which ended after a 1998 peace deal.

Donaldson was central to the negotiation of a crucial post-Brexit trade deal with the United Kingdom government two months before his arrest.

It enabled the end of the DUP’s two-year boycott of the devolved power-sharing assembly at Stormont and had also been expected to lead his party into the next UK general election.

Donaldson was knighted by the late Queen Elizabeth for his political services in 2016.

He asked for his knighthood to be renounced two days after his conviction.

The jury also found that Donaldson’s wife, Eleanor, ‌‌aided and ‌‌abetted her husband. She has also denied the charges.

The court ruled her unfit to stand trial last month due to mental health issues, meaning she could not face criminal conviction.

articles.title: Comedian Bert Kreischer compares perfect burger to great sex: 'Doesn't need to be fancy'
articles.summary: Comedian Bert Kreischer shares his burger preference, his smash burger obsession and why Guy Fieri's Carnival cruise burger bar serves the best burger he's ever had.
articles.body: Comedian Bert Kreischer knows a thing or two about burgers — and his recipe for the perfect one is surprisingly simple, even if his description is anything but family-friendly. "A good burger is like great sex. It doesn't need to be fancy," Kreischer said in an interview ahead of his appearance as host of the Burger Bash at Thursday night's New York City Wine & Food Festival. For Kreischer, the ideal burger doesn't require exotic ingredients or elaborate toppings. He prefers the classics: a buttery, toasted brioche bun, American cheese and traditional fixings. WAHLBURGERS CHEF PAUL WAHLBERG SHARES SIMPLE RULES FOR GRILLING PERFECT MEMORIAL DAY BURGER "I've got to be in a mood to have a raspberry jam and goat cheese on a burger," he told Fox News Digital. The comedian's passion for burgers goes well beyond punchlines. On his cooking show, "Something's Burning," Kreischer became so proficient at making smash burgers that he found himself eating them around the clock. "I got so good at making smash burgers that I went through a smash burger phase where I was having them for breakfast, lunch and dinner," he recalled. STOP MAKING A COMMON BURGER MISTAKE, CHEF WARNS: 'ONE OF THE WORST THINGS YOU CAN DO' Eventually, Kreischer said, he had to stop making them so frequently. But one burger still holds a special place in his heart: the one served at Guy Fieri's burger bar aboard Carnival cruise ships. "The best thing Guy Fieri has ever done in his life is the f------ Guy Fieri burger bar on the cruise ships," Kreischer said. "That is the best burger you'll ever have." He particularly appreciates the generous portions, the option to double up on patties and cheese, and the freedom to customize his burger with whatever toppings he wants. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Kreischer, who is preparing to host his own Fully Loaded at Sea comedy cruise featuring a live taping of "Something's Burning," said he'd happily spend an afternoon making burgers behind the counter if the ship had a Guy Fieri burger bar. For now, his attention is on Burger Bash, where some of the country's top burger makers will compete for bragging rights. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Although Kreischer has no shortage of opinions about what makes a winning burger, he's relieved that his role is to host rather than judge, as he did earlier this year at the South Beach Wine & Food Festival. "Yeah, it's so much better than judging it," he said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP For Kreischer, the best burgers aren't necessarily the most adventurous. articles.title: Why Harry and Meghan's UK relaunch felt so much like a royal engagement
articles.summary: The Duchess of Sussex has not done anything like the day of events in Nottingham for several years on British soil.
articles.body:
There was something so very familiar about today.

The first time the Duke and Duchess of Sussex visited Nottingham together in 2017 they were plain old Prince Harry and Meghan Markle. They'd just announced they were getting married and it was in the East Midlands that an American actress would be hard launched as a working member of the Royal Family.

You could view today as the UK-relaunch of Meghan.

She'd not done anything like the day of events in Nottingham for several years on British soil. Those close to her told me she wasn't nervous about how people would react to her and she wanted to get out there.

This was definitely not a royal engagement.

But the thing is, it felt like one in so many ways.

There was planned choreography for each event.

Harry and Meghan visited charities and met volunteers.

There was a shared media pool working together to distribute the best video and images.

Buckingham Palace has made it very clear that they view the Duke and Duchess of Sussex as private citizens. Whatever they do is their own business - but it certainly won't have royal status attached.

There was no pomp and ceremony today. No line up of dignitaries. No obvious police presence.

It was still a reminder of what Harry and Meghan have to offer.

Meghan makes first official public appearance since moving back to UK

Meghan shares glimpse of family life after Sussexes return to UK

Much of the crowd that came out to see them was young and diverse - the vast majority of people I saw were under 30.

The mood at each event was informal with a strong emphasis on getting stuck in. They baked cupcakes, made West African food, played pool and had a go at basketball.

Watching both Harry and Meghan up close is a reminder of their ease at these kind of charity events. It plays to their strengths and Meghan brings that air of American self confidence.

Their return has unsettled the Royal Family with King Charles III just getting a few days notice ahead of the news breaking in August that the Sussexes were coming back to the UK with their children Archie and Lilibet.

While his son and daughter-in-law were in Nottingham, the King was at the ceremonial opening of the Senedd in Cardiff, firmly on royal duty, delivering a speech rich in references to community, to character and identity with an overriding message of the power of endurance.

And the complexity of the Harry and Meghan story is requiring endurance on all sides.

I get lots of messages and emails asking me why the BBC covers Harry and Meghan if they are not working members of the royal family.

The answer is because they have contributed to one of the most turbulent periods in the Royal Family in recent times and our audiences are interested whether they love or loathe the Sussexes.

And on a personal level, they remind us all how painful family breakdown can be and the deep damage it can cause to family life with the blame and bitterness hard to resolve - even more so when much of it is being played out in public.

We will continue to report on the work of all senior royals. Later this month, the King goes on an important trip to the Caribbean and the Prince of Wales will be in India next month with his Earthshot environmental prize. Both trips will provide insights into the priorities of father and son

The joint Harry and Meghan event we saw in Nottingham won't be a regular occurrence but will happen occasionally. The Sussex's representatives have stressed that they both have their own separate interests to focus on with plans for Meghan to launch a UK version of her lifestyle brand As Ever - possibly before Christmas.

And talking of Christmas - don't expect to see Harry and Meghan in Sandringham with the rest of the Royal Family. They will instead spend that time with Meghan's mother, Doria Ragland, possibly here in the UK.

Families are complicated. The return of Harry and Meghan is a clear reminder of that.

Charity? Acting? The Cotswolds? What will Harry and Meghan's UK life look like?

Prince Harry says it is 'great' to be back in Britain after six years in US

What happened to Harry and Meghan's American dream?

articles.title: When should you clean your gutters? Experts share the best time
articles.summary: Clean your gutters too early and you’ll have to do it again, wait too long and they could overflow. Experts explain when to clean them and how to do it.
articles.body: With all the content available online these days, it can be hard to figure out what’s real and what’s hype. While we don’t always have the answers, we have a direct line to people who do — which is why we present to you our series The Internet Made Me Ask, where we have experts break down the truth about some of the buzziest trends (and questions) on our timelines, like how often you should wash jeans. Cleaning your gutters is one of those fall chores where timing is everything. Do it too early, and you’ll likely find yourself back on the ladder a few weeks later once the rest of the leaves come down. If you wait too long, you risk clogged gutters overflowing during a rainstorm, which can lead to water damage around your roof, siding, and foundation. So when exactly is the sweet spot? I spoke to two experts to find out when you should clean your gutters and how to do it safely and effectively. When is the right time to clean your gutters? The best way to tell if it is time to clean your gutters is to look at the trees around your yard. “Ideally, you want to do a major clean right after the majority of the leaves have fallen — usually late autumn,” says Zack Nienaber, owner of Nienaber and Sons Lawn Care in Cincinnati. “If you do it too early before the trees shed, you’ll just end up having to do it all over again once the rest drops.” That said, the exact timing depends on where you live and what kinds of trees surround your home, which is why you really need to let your yard be your guide rather than the calendar. Once the branches overhead look mostly bare, it’s time to get to work. Just don’t put it off for too long: Gutters packed with leaves can’t drain properly, so the next heavy rain could send water spilling over the sides — and the U.S. has been seeing a lot of rain this season, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). What do you need to clean your gutters? Cleaning your gutters probably isn’t anyone’s idea of a fun weekend, but it doesn’t have to be miserable, either. I’m sharing expert steps on how to do it below, but first, here are some tools that can make the job faster, safer, and a lot less messy. These are the types of tools the experts I spoke to suggest having on hand before you start. A good extension ladder will help you reach the gutters, says Nienaber. This fiberglass extension ladder reaches up to 21 feet when fully extended, giving you enough height to get to second-story gutters. It supports up to 300 pounds and has slip-resistant, D-shaped rungs to help you keep your footing while you work. The swivel safety shoes at the base help keep the ladder steady. One helpful tip: “Don’t lean the ladder against the gutters — it can bend or crush them,” says Nienaber. “Instead, rest it against the roof.” Nienaber says a plastic gutter scooper can help you get debris out while protecting your hands. This one is made from high-impact polypropylene and has a deep, curved scoop that lets you grab big clumps of wet leaves at once. It also has an ergonomic handle and fits most gutters, according to the brand. Gloves protect your hands from sharp twigs, rough gutter edges, and all the wet muck you’ll be scooping out. This pair has padded synthetic leather palms that help you keep a firm grip on your ladder and tools, plus a stretchy, breathable back so your hands stay comfortable. They’re also flexible enough that you can handle a scoop or hose. If you’d rather stay off a ladder, this cordless leaf blower comes with a 4.5-foot attachment that lets you clear leaves from your gutters while standing on the ground. It has a brushless motor with two speed settings. The kit also comes with two 40-volt batteries and a charger. How to clean your gutters Take time to set up your station: Before you start pulling out leaves, set yourself up to work safely. “Make sure your ladder is on stable, level ground,” says Nienaber, who also suggests wearing thick gloves. “I then like to scoop the debris out by hand into a bucket rather than blasting everything down the downspout (the vertical pipe that goes from gutter to ground) and packing it solid.” Create a game plan for the process: Where you start matters, too. “Begin at the downspout and proceed to the far end of the gutter — this way, you will clear the downspout opening first and prevent yourself from pushing debris into it,” says Constantine Anest, owner of Ethos Roofing & Restoration in Denver.Rinse last: After you’ve removed the leaves and twigs, finish with a rinse. “Once the bulk is out, flush the system with a hose to make sure the water flows freely through the spouts,” says Nienaber. articles.title: Washington state's high school sports league puts onus for trans athlete controversy on state laws
articles.summary: The WIAA says Washington state law prevents it from banning males from girls' sports, even if members vote for change. Initiative 638 heads to voters.
articles.body: Washington state has been rocked in recent weeks by a controversy involving a male cross-country runner who switched from a boys’ team to a girls’ team mid-season. The controversy culminated in a protest Tuesday, when about a dozen female runners for Camas High School walked off the course, refusing to compete with their new male teammate. The association governing Washington school sports says state law prevents it from implementing the proposed changes to its participation policy. In a statement to OutKick, the Washington Interscholastic Activities Association (WIAA) said it cannot adopt a new policy to keep males out of girls’ sports, even if its members vote for a policy change, as it would be "in violation of Washington state law." DAD BANNED FROM SCHOOL GROUNDS AFTER PROTESTING TRANS RUNNER COMPETING AGAINST HIS DAUGHTER "In the last two years, through the association’s amendment process, three amendments have been proposed to alter the gender-identity participation policies. Those amendments did not meet the 60% threshold to pass. Nevertheless, even if the amendments had met the threshold and passed, the WIAA cannot implement a policy that is in violation of Washington state law and the amendments proposed would have violated state law. If state law changes, the WIAA Executive Board will revise policies as necessary to remain in compliance with state law," part of the WIAA’s statement read. Washington voters are set to decide whether to change the rules next month. Initiative 638, which would prohibit biological male students from competing in certain female-only school sports and require a healthcare provider's verification of biological sex, will be on the state ballot on Nov. 3. Democrats currently hold majorities in both chambers of the state legislature and control the governor’s office. Democratic Gov. Bob Ferguson has expressed opposition to Initiative 638. WHERE TOP DEMOCRAT SENATE CANDIDATES AND THEIR GOP OPPONENTS STAND ON TRANS ATHLETES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS "Washingtonians should know that I-638 won’t create opportunities for girls, but it will force them into invasive sex verification exams in order to participate in sports," Ferguson said in a statement published Sept. 29 by the opposition campaign, No Hate in WA State. The measure reached the ballot after lawmakers took no action on it during the 2026 session. Earlier this year, Democratic legislative leaders said they would leave the decision to voters. The vote will come as the state grapples with multiple controversies involving males in girls’ sports, including the Camas cross-country runner and a separate incident involving a transgender wrestler who allegedly sexually assaulted a female athlete during a match last December, according to the female athlete’s lawsuit. Prosecutors declined to file criminal charges in that case. In its statement to OutKick, the WIAA described itself as a membership-driven association whose members create its rules. It said its gender-identity participation policy has been in place since the 2007-08 school year and was adopted to align with Washington law. "The WIAA is a membership-driven association. The membership creates the rules found in the WIAA Handbook. The gender-identity participation policies found in the WIAA Handbook at Rule 18.16.0 have been in place for 20 years, since the 2007-08 school year. The rules were passed to align with Washington state law. The WIAA remains committed to following Washington state law … which permits student-athletes to participate in sports consistent with the gender with which they identify," the statement read. "WIAA Handbook 18.16.0 states that school personnel will work collaboratively with the student to determine eligibility, however, a timeline for switching teams is not designated. WIAA Handbook 17.11 establishes practice regulations, outlining the minimum number of practice requirements. WIAA Handbook 18.2.1 demonstrates that student’s must be deemed eligible by the respective sport’s 50% date in order to be eligible to participate in postseason competition. "The WIAA Handbook provides the framework for schools, leagues, and WIAA Districts to operate events throughout the year. The WIAA Office does not manage day-to-day league and WIAA District events and instead is tasked with running WIAA State Tournaments. For example, the WIAA Office establishes signage policies for WIAA State events, but not league or WIAA District contests. Once again, the WIAA is a membership-driven association." After the U.S. Supreme Court upheld other states’ laws restricting transgender athletes’ participation in girls’ and women’s sports in landmark rulings in June, Washington’s Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction (OSPI) said the decisions did not change Washington law. The agency said Superintendent Chris Reykdal would continue enforcing state law allowing students to compete consistent with their gender identity. "Today’s decision reinforces Washington state’s ability to adopt and implement our own laws in alignment with our values," Reykdal said in the June 30 statement. The distinction matters for families seeking a different policy: a ruling allowing states to restrict participation does not itself enact such a restriction in Washington. Initiative 638 would require school districts and covered athletic associations to prohibit students it defines as biologically male from competing with or against female students in certain competitions intended for female students only. It would apply to individual and team events. Students entering those competitions would have to provide a signed statement from a personal healthcare provider verifying biological sex through reproductive anatomy, genetic makeup or naturally produced testosterone levels. Backers, led by Let’s Go Washington, say the measure would preserve fair competition and opportunities for girls. They argue that transgender students would retain opportunities to participate in sports in categories corresponding to their sex. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Opponents say the measure would exclude transgender girls and create new medical and privacy burdens for girls seeking to play school sports. Supporters dispute Ferguson’s characterization of the verification requirement. Let’s Go Washington says the measure does not mandate genital examinations and that verification could occur through the existing sports-physical process. The political decision to leave the initiative for voters was clear months before the Camas protest. In January, Senate Majority Leader Jamie Pedersen and House Speaker Laurie Jinkins said they did not plan to hold hearings on the sports initiative and a separate parental-rights measure, according to the Washington State Standard. "They’ll be up to the voters to decide."

articles.title: Cornell president faces contentious faculty senate meeting over Jane Doe allegations
articles.summary: Cornell University’s president was met with scrutiny and sharp questions from its faculty senate on Wednesday, when the group convened to discuss a no-confidence vote over the university’s handling of an alleged 2024 sexual assault at a fraternity house, according to an audio recording obtained by NBC News.
articles.body: Cornell University’s president was met with scrutiny and sharp questions from its faculty senate on Wednesday, when the group convened to discuss a no-confidence vote over the university’s handling of an alleged 2024 sexual assault at a fraternity house, according to an audio recording obtained by NBC News. Discussion of a no-confidence vote comes after serious concerns were raised by students and staff over how the university responded to the allegations. University President Michael Kotlikoff defended himself and Cornell’s administration as he took a series of pointed questions from the school staff. At the meeting, most speakers were heard identifying themselves before speaking. Risa Lieberwitz, a professor of labor and employment law, said the issue of sexual assault “is a systemic problem. It deserves systemic attention.” She told Kotlikoff that thus far it appeared he had “simply reacted to pressure.” “It feels that the administration is considering more about how do we respond to pressure rather than the kind of leadership, which should have been doing systemic work and prioritizing these issues all along,” she said. Kotlikoff argued that replacing its leadership was not the solution. “We need to be able to work together to be able to change the culture, educate our students, and try and address this problem,” he said at the meeting. “I want Cornell to be a leader in this area, and we have plans to really invest in this area. But the idea that you can somehow, because an event has occurred, eliminate it immediately — it’s just unrealistic.” Last month, a former student identified as Jane Doe sued the university and seven current and former students in connection with her allegation of sexual assault. In 2024, Cornell shut down the Chi Phi fraternity chapter at the university and expelled two students after Doe reported the incident. Others were suspended or faced lesser disciplinary action. The university also said it launched the Presidential Task Force on Campus Sexual Assault shortly after the incident and implemented recommendations to address sexual assault on campus. No criminal charges were brought at the time, and the investigation has been reopened following Jane Doe’s lawsuit. Four of the men, through their attorneys, have denied coercing Jane Doe with drugs or sexually assaulting her. NBC News was not able to reach the other three men named in the lawsuit. While the faculty senate does not have the authority to remove the president, the move would greatly increase the pressure on Cornell and its administration. Darlene Evans, a senior lecturer emerita, asked Kotlikoff why he was only taking steps now “towards serious systemic change” when he had been in leadership roles at the university for more than a decade. Evans noted that more than 35% of female undergraduates surveyed at Cornell University reported experiencing nonconsensual sexual contact involving physical force, threats of force or incapacitation, according to a Cornell University poll conducted last year, a figure that was up from 23% in 2023. “It wasn’t until a no-confidence vote was introduced that Cornell’s administration announced any real steps to prevent sexual assault on this campus, or to seriously support survivors,” she said. “So saying what we’re going to do now kind of rings hollow here. Why haven’t you taken these things more seriously until now, when there’s a firestorm of press looking at Cornell?” Kotlikoff announced on Tuesday that all parties at fraternity houses and events would be banned through the rest of the academic year. “We don’t have full ability to be confident that what goes on in those houses is safe and so for the time being we will stop that activity,” he said during the meeting on Wednesday. He also addressed calls from some over whether Greek life at the university should be banned altogether. “If at the end of the day, fraternities cannot exist in a safe environment, and we can’t be convinced that they can be safe, then we should make that decision,” he said. “But we should make it based on data and study and expertise, not on emotion.” After a question-and-answer session, the faculty senate began debating the no-confidence resolution, with another meeting scheduled for later this month. Many spoke in favor of the resolution, while others wanted to delay the vote until the results of an upcoming independent investigation. Earlier this month, the university announced that Sally Yates, the former deputy U.S. attorney general and acting U.S. attorney general, would lead an independent review on how Cornell University responded to the allegations and, more broadly, how it responds to sexual harassment, assault and misconduct on campus. New York Attorney General Letitia James is also investigating the allegation. A spokesperson said staff members from the attorney general’s office have “spoken with the Tompkins County District Attorney, Jane Doe’s attorney, and several candidates for outside counsel to support the investigation.” After the meeting, music professor Ariana Kim said she was “really inspired by everyone who spoke and was brave in favor of the resolution — it takes a lot to stand up in front of the president and ask direct questions of him.” Kim said she has received some 200 emails from alumni saying they support the no-confidence resolution and want the administration to be held accountable. The professor said some at the meeting held up signs that read, “I stand with Jane Doe,” “How many more?” and “We demand accountability.” “Some people broke down and held each other after the meeting,” she said. Political history professor Richard Bensel said that so far the central administration “has not responded in a way that is going to diminish faculty and students’ despair over the way that the university has treated the issue.” Bensel said he was unsure if he wanted the president to resign, but said he thought university leadership “will not reform itself without passage of the no-confidence resolution.” “I can imagine a way the trustees through the president can reconcile their relations with the Cornell community but that requires a real change in governance style and I don’t think that is possible under this administration,” he said. “There are real problems in the way the university is run.”

articles.title: Active shooter report at Oregon elementary school draws large police response
articles.summary: Bend police responded to Silver Rail Elementary School after an active shooter report, directing families to a nearby church for reunification.
articles.body: Police rushed to an Oregon elementary school Thursday after a report of an active shooter, urging the public to stay away as families were directed to a nearby church. The Bend Police Department said officers were at Silver Rail Elementary School, where a large police presence gathered as authorities responded. "The Bend Police Department is currently at Silver Rail Elementary School after a report of an active shooter," the department said in a statement. "There is a large police presence in the area. Please avoid the area." REPORTED SHOOTING AT VIRGINIA ELEMENTARY SCHOOL 'CONTAINED,' SHERIFF'S OFFICE SAYS Authorities directed students’ families to Journey Church at 61303 S. Highway 97, near Goodwill and Dairy Queen, which was designated as the family reunification location. Police had not immediately released information about injuries or a possible suspect. It was not immediately clear whether authorities had confirmed gunfire at the school. "We will share more information as soon as we can," the department said. Sen. articles.title: Bus hits train stopped on French side of  Channel Tunnel, with 19 injured
articles.summary: Two people were severely injured and evacuated by helicopter but no one's life appeared to be in danger, officials said.
articles.body:
A bus has hit a stationary freight train near the French entrance to the Channel Tunnel, injuring the driver and 18 passengers, the French authorities say.

The bus, which was carrying lorry drivers due to take a shuttle rail service, struck the train at the loading platform of the tunnel in Coquelles, near Calais.

Two people were severely injured and evacuated by helicopter though no one's life appeared to be in danger, a local official said.

Local sub-prefect Agathe Cury said that freight traffic and Eurostar passenger traffic through the tunnel had not been disrupted by the incident, which occurred at 19:27 (17:27 GMT), apart from a brief stoppage to allow the injured to be evacuated.

Those involved in the crash are all men and of different nationalities, she added.

Photos published by local French newspaper La Voix du Nord show a small bus with damage to its front and side standing alongside a train, among a crowd of emergency workers.

Eurostar released an update saying: "An incident occurred several kilometers away from the Channel Tunnel.

"This incident does not involved or impact Eurostar trains running from and to London. All of Eurostar trains will run as expected."
